$schema_note: The Tawked Account API as the SDKs build on it. Generated by sdks/contract/generate.php --surface=account from App\AccountApi\OpenApiDocument and App\AccountApi\Operations; do not edit by hand.

envelope.error: Error below; a 428 approval_required carries approval and human_action

account_writes.replay: The same key and the same request answer the stored 2xx with Idempotent-Replayed: true, for 24 hours.
account_writes.release: Any throwable or non-2xx deletes the key (App\Http\Middleware\AccountApiIdempotency): every write is write_once in the SDKs.
account_writes.secret: An answer carrying plaintext, secret or client_secret, or an operation marked secret, is never kept: its replay answers 409 idempotency_secret_not_replayable with the id of what it made.
account_writes.approval: A 428 approval_required is never stored: send the approved request again with the same key and Tawked-Approval.

approvals.resend: the same method, path, body and Idempotency-Key, with Tawked-Approval: <approval id>

error.description: A snake_case code: validation_failed, insufficient_permission, forbidden, not_found, rate_limited, ip_not_allowed, approval_required, approval_mismatch, approval_declined, approval_expired, approval_used, approval_stale, or the operation's own.

fields.description: On validation_failed: each field and what to fix.

needs.description: On insufficient_permission: the permission the token lacks.

next.description: Always: the sentence naming what to call next (relay human_action, fix the named fields, list the ids this token reaches, wait and retry).

did_you_mean.description: On an operation or a path no route answers, and on a wrong method: the operations meant, each with its id, method and path.

HumanAction.description: Only a person can move this forward: tell them `say`, give them `url`, and once they say it is done call the operation `then`.

url.description: Absolute, in the language of `say`: the exact page they open.

say.description: The sentence to relay to the person: in the request's Accept-Language when it sends one, else in the person's own language.

then.description: The operation id to call once the person is done.

Approval.description: A consequential call waiting for its person's yes in the console. Read approvals.show until `approved`, then send exactly the same request again with Tawked-Approval: <id>.

endpoints.summary: The alerts this person may read, newest first (an application approved or rejected, a template rejected, a low balance…), each with its kind, data, whether they read it and whether it waits on them (`needs`).
endpoints.description: Filters: `status` (unread or needs), `application` (an application id), `group` (a kind group). Paged by `limit` and `cursor`. A token chosen for some applications reads only the alerts about them, as a member scoped to them would (never one about the account as a whole, the balance among them).

endpoints.summary: Mark one alert read for this person (others still see it unread); answers ok.
Mark every alert this person may read as read, for them alone; answers ok with how many were marked.

Save the account's business document alone: `business_document_type` (commercial_registration or freelance_certificate) and its `business_document_number`; the owner's alone. Answers the account as account.show does.
endpoints.description: Verify needs it: until the account holds one, applications.products.add and applications.applications.create answer 409 `business_document_missing` for `verify`. The type and the number are the person's to give: ask them, never guess. A member gets 403: only the owner saves it.

endpoints.summary: Confirm the pending business e-mail with the code the person received; with `application`, Verify is then turned on for that application. Answers the account as account.show does, and `verify_turned_on_for`.
endpoints.description: Refusals: 409 `nothing_pending` (send a code first, or it was sent over an hour ago), 422 `code_invalid`, 429 `too_many_attempts` (send a new code) or `rate_limited`, 409 `email_taken`. An `application` this person may not edit is ignored.

endpoints.summary: Drop the business e-mail waiting for its code (to send a code to another address); answers ok.

Send a six-digit code to the business e-mail (an address on the business's own domain); answers the address now pending and when another code may be asked for. The person reads the code and you call account.email.confirm.
endpoints.description: The owner's. Refusals: 422 `email_refused` with `reason` (personal, invalid, no_mailbox), 409 `email_taken`, 429 `send_cooldown` / `daily_limit` / `rate_limited`, 503 `unavailable`. The code arrives by e-mail to the address: only the person can read it, so relay `human_action` and send what they tell you to account.email.confirm.

endpoints.summary: Save this person's own name and e-mail (a member; the owner saves theirs with account.profile.update). Answers the account as account.show does.
Save the account's profile (contact name, contact e-mail, business document); the owner's alone. Answers the account as account.show does.
endpoints.description: On an account that uses Verify the contact e-mail changes only through its code: send a new address with account.email.send, then account.email.confirm (a different address here answers 409 `business_email_unconfirmed`; leave it out or send the current one). 409 `email_taken` when another person holds the address. A member gets 403: they save their own with account.me.update.

endpoints.summary: Sign this person out of every console session on every device, and out of the AI assistants they signed in; this token keeps working. Answers ok.
endpoints.description: Tawked Chat keeps its own sign-in. Account API tokens are not touched: revoke one with account.tokens.revoke.

endpoints.summary: The account as Settings shows it to this person: the profile (owner only), their own name, e-mail and phone, their role, and the business e-mail's state (confirmed, or a code pending).

The last calls made with an Account API token, newest first: the operation, method and path, the status and error code, the address, the client (user agent), the assistant when it came through the MCP server, and how long it took. Kept 90 days. Your own tokens, or any of the account's for the owner.
endpoints.description: Pages with `limit` (up to 50) and `cursor`. Never the input or the answer of a call. A token you do not see answers 404.

endpoints.summary: The Account API tokens this person may see (their own; the owner sees every token of the account), newest first: name, prefix, permissions, applications, who made it, last use, expiry and revocation. Never the secret.
Revoke an Account API token: the next call made with it answers 401. Your own, or any of the account's for the owner. Answers the token, revoked.
endpoints.description: Revoking the token this call is made with is allowed and ends this connection. Revoking twice changes nothing.

endpoints.summary: Appeal Tawked's rejection of the application with a `note` (and optionally a multipart `document`, up to 10 MB): it goes back to review; answers the application and `next`.
endpoints.description: Only while `review.appeal.state` is `available` (within the window after a rejection by Tawked); otherwise 409 `appeal_<state>`. 422 `note_required` or `document_type`.

endpoints.summary: Create an application (names in Arabic and English, website, industry, products); it enters Tawked's review at once and answers the application with its state and `next` (read applications.applications.show every few hours until the review ends).
endpoints.description: The names reach customers in every code and message, so Tawked screens and reviews them: `state` is `review` (or `review_flagged` when a person must look) until Tawked decides; read it again with applications.applications.show. Choosing `verify` needs the account's business e-mail confirmed (409 `business_email_unconfirmed`), then its business document on file (409 `business_document_missing`: account.document.update). 409 `application_limit_reached` when the account holds as many as it may.

endpoints.summary: Delete the application, its name typed to confirm (`confirm_name`, Arabic or English): every key is revoked, its own WhatsApp number disconnected. Cannot be undone.
endpoints.description: 422 `name_mismatch` when `confirm_name` is neither name; 409 `staff_number` when Tawked's team connected its number; 503 `disconnect_failed` when the number could not be disconnected (nothing is deleted). The first two are answered before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: List the applications this token reaches, newest first: names, logo, products, status and state (working, review, review_flagged, rejected, suspended, paused, disabled, withdrawn), the decision's words, what the person may do.

Apply again after withdrawing: the application goes back into Tawked's review queue and the team is told; answers the application and `next` (read applications.applications.show until the review ends).
One application as its Details page shows it, with its review history: where the review stands, a rejection's reason and appeal, Verify's pause, its WhatsApp number.
Lift the pause Verify's pumping guard put on the application (its `paused`), once the spike was looked at; codes go out again. Answers the application.
Save the application's details (both names, website, industry; optionally `remove_logo`): answers the application, whether the change sent it back to Tawked's review, and `next`.
endpoints.description: Send every field, as the Details form does. A change of a name or the website goes back to review (`sent_to_review`); the logo never does (upload it with applications.logo.upload). 409 `under_appeal` while Tawked reads an appeal.

endpoints.summary: Withdraw the application's review request: it leaves Tawked's queue until applications.applications.reapply; answers the application.
endpoints.description: Only while it waits in review (`review.may_withdraw`); otherwise 409 `invalid_transition`.

endpoints.summary: Create a Sending API key for the application (`mode` live or test, `name`, `access` full or custom with `scopes` per product, `expires_in_days`, `ip_allowlist`; Email `manage`, `webhooks` true to manage the application's webhook endpoints (the `webhooks:manage` scope), `email_domain_id` for a sending key limited to one domain, `inbound` true to let it read received email (opt-in, live keys only)); answers the key with its `plaintext`, shown this once.
endpoints.description: Store the plaintext at once: it is never answered again (applications.keys.list shows the prefix). A test key reaches only the sandbox; a live key needs the application not rejected or suspended (409 `application_not_active`). A test key grants nothing on WhatsApp (422) and on Email reads and sends in test mode only (never `manage`, never `webhooks`). A full-access key never manages Email nor the webhooks: they are granted by name. `email_domain_id` takes a live key whose only grant is Email `send` (422 `validation_failed` on `email_domain_id` otherwise). The key never reaches beyond this token: full access needs `verify:write`, `whatsapp:write` and `email:write`, a product's send its area's write, a read its read (else 403 `insufficient_permission` with `missing`).

endpoints.summary: List the application's Sending API keys, newest first, live and test, revoked ones too: prefix, mode, what each may call, allowlist, last used. Never a secret.

Revoke one of the application's keys: every call with it is refused from now on (a connected app's key also ends that connection). Cannot be undone. Answers ok; make a new one with applications.keys.create.
Remove the application's logo; answers the application.
Upload the application's logo (multipart field `logo`, PNG or JPEG); answers the application with its `logo_url`. A logo never sends it back to review.
Turn a product on for the application (`product`: verify, notifications, chat or email); answers the application. Turning one on is intent: each product's own setup follows.
endpoints.description: 409 `business_email_unconfirmed` for `verify` until the account's business e-mail is confirmed, then 409 `business_document_missing` until it holds a business document (account.document.update). `then` is the console's own and changes nothing here.

endpoints.summary: The application's webhook delivery log, newest first, narrowed by `status` (pending, delivered, failed), `event` and `endpoint`: each with its attempts, last HTTP code and error, and the payload sent.
Send a delivered or failed webhook delivery again, as a new delivery to the same endpoint with the same payload and the same event id (your server dedupes on it); answers the new delivery.
endpoints.description: Only a final delivery (409 `delivery_pending` while it is still retried), while its endpoint is there and on (409 `endpoint_unavailable`). A window of deliveries: applications.webhooks.replay.

endpoints.summary: Add a webhook endpoint (`url` https on a public host, `events`, optionally `receives_test`); answers it with its signing `secret` and its Standard Webhooks `standard_secret`, shown this once.
endpoints.description: Up to five endpoints (409 `endpoint_limit_reached`, before any approval is asked). Every delivery is signed with the endpoint's secret (`tawked-signature`) and with Standard Webhooks (`webhook-signature`, the `standard_secret`); verify either on your server. `receives_test: true` lets test-mode e-mail events reach it. Send a test with applications.webhooks.test.

endpoints.summary: Delete a webhook endpoint: nothing more is sent to it, and a delivery still waiting stops. Its past deliveries stay in the log (applications.webhook_deliveries.list). Answers ok.
List the application's webhook endpoints (address, events, on or off, `state` receiving/failing/off, last delivery), with the events it may subscribe to and the most endpoints it may hold.

Send an endpoint's deliveries of a window again (`since`, `until` at most 7 days later and within the last 30 days, `status` failed or all, optional `events`), at most 1,000 oldest first, each with its own event id; answers the replay, queued.
endpoints.description: One replay of an endpoint at a time (409 `replay_running`); the endpoint must be on (409 `endpoint_off`). Read its progress with applications.webhooks.replays.show.

endpoints.summary: One replay of a webhook endpoint: its `state` (queued, running, done), how many deliveries `matched` and how many were `queued` again, its window.
Answer a webhook endpoint's current signing secret (`secret`); every reveal is recorded.

Give a webhook endpoint a new signing secret by `scheme`: `tawked` (the default) a new `tawked-signature` secret, the old one stopping at once, answered as `secret`; `standard` a new Standard Webhooks secret, the old one still signing beside it for 24 hours; or `both`. Answers the new `secrets` once.
endpoints.description: The answer is `{id, secret?, secrets: {standard?, tawked?}, previous_valid_until, tawked_switched_at}`; `secret` is the new tawked secret, there whenever it was rotated (as before `scheme` existed). A tawked rotation has no grace: update your server at once. `standard` turns Standard signing on for an endpoint that had none.

endpoints.summary: One webhook endpoint: its address, events, whether it receives, its state and last delivery. Its secret only through applications.webhooks.reveal_secret.

Send a test delivery of one of the endpoint's events (`event`, else its first) to it, marked `"test": true`, with sample data; answers the queued delivery. Read its outcome in applications.webhook_deliveries.list.
endpoints.description: 409 `endpoint_off` while the endpoint is switched off; 422 when `event` is not one the endpoint receives.

endpoints.summary: Change a webhook endpoint: its `url` and `events` (both sent, as the form does) and, optionally, `enabled` to switch it off or on, `receives_test` and `signing.standard_webhooks`; the secrets stay. Answers the endpoint, with its new `standard_secret` once when Standard signing is turned on for the first time.
endpoints.description: Switching on an endpoint we switched off after five days of failure (`state` disabled_failing) clears its failing state. Turning Standard Webhooks signing on adds the `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` headers to its deliveries; give your verifier the `standard_secret`.

endpoints.summary: List the approvals this token asked its person for, newest first, each with its status (pending, approved, used, declined, expired, stale), operation, request, `target` (the draft it acts on, as the person saw it) and expiry.

Read one approval this token asked for: its status, what it covers (the request, and `target`: the campaign, automation, auto-attendant, template draft or Radeef it acts on, as the person saw it) and `next`, what to do in that status. Once it is `approved`, send exactly the same request again with the header `Tawked-Approval: <id>`; it runs once.
endpoints.description: A consequential call (it reaches customers, spends, deletes or cannot be undone) of a token whose approvals are on answers HTTP 428 `approval_required` with `approval` and a `human_action` (`approve_request`): give the person its link and its `say`, then read this until the status moves. `pending`: the person has not decided yet. `approved`: send the request again with `Tawked-Approval`. `declined`: do not send it again unless the person asks. `expired`: ask again (24 hours from the ask). `used`: it already ran. `stale`: the draft it acts on was edited after the ask (the approval covers the draft as the person saw it, never a later edit): send the request again without Tawked-Approval to ask about what it holds now.

endpoints.summary: Create an automation, off: from a ready-made one (`recipe`, its draft prefilled) or empty without one. Answers the automation with its draft; then save the draft (automations.automations.update), try it (automations.automations.send_test) and turn it on (automations.automations.on).
endpoints.description: recipe: a key from automations.recipes.list. Errors: recipe_unavailable 409 (it needs the application's Salla store), recipe_locked 409 (the store's own notice covers the same event: switch it off first; `notice` names it).

endpoints.summary: Delete an automation: its live runs stop now, its history stays. Answers ok.
List the application's WhatsApp automations, newest first: each on or off, what it starts on (its trigger), whether the draft differs from what runs, and its last publish.
Turn an automation off: no run starts; a waiting run finishes the wait it is in and stops there unless it is on again by then. Answers the automation.
Turn an automation on: the draft is published first when it differs, then runs start from now for each contact its trigger meets, messaging customers. Answers the automation.
endpoints.description: Each error is answered before any approval is asked: definition_invalid 422 (`problems`: [{step, code}]), whatsapp_not_connected 409, meta_unavailable 502.

endpoints.summary: Publish the draft as the version new runs start on (runs under way keep theirs). Answers the automation; 422 definition_invalid with each problem when it cannot run.
endpoints.description: On an automation that is on, this changes what customers receive from now. Each error is answered before any approval is asked: definition_invalid 422 (`problems`: [{step, code}]), whatsapp_not_connected 409, meta_unavailable 502.

endpoints.summary: Run the draft as it is now on your own Saudi mobile (the token's person), every wait one minute, labelled a test; answers the test run, to read in its log.
endpoints.description: At most 5 tests in 10 minutes. Each error is answered before any approval is asked: no_phone 422, definition_invalid 422 (`problems`), whatsapp_not_connected 409, meta_unavailable 502.

endpoints.summary: One automation: its draft and its published definition whole, on or off, its version, what keeps the draft from running (`problems`, each with its step and code), the Salla notice it would repeat, and its last 30 days (live, completed, stopped, failed runs; messages sent).

Save an automation's draft (its trigger, conditions and steps) and its name: nothing is checked beyond the shape, and what runs does not change until it is published. Answers the automation with the draft's problems; once there are none, try it with automations.automations.send_test and publish it with automations.automations.publish (or automations.automations.on).
endpoints.description: definition: {trigger: {kind, …, reentry}, conditions: [], steps: [{id, kind: wait|send|wait_reply|add_tag|remove_tag|assign|…, …}]}, the shape automations.automations.show answers in `draft` (start from a ready-made one to see it). Up to 10 steps. A ready-made automation's templates go to Meta on this save.

endpoints.summary: List the ready-made automations (welcome, abandoned cart, win-back, review request…) with their trigger, whether this application may use them (the Salla ones need its store) and, when the store's own notice covers the event, that notice (`locked_by`). The whole catalogue in one answer (no paging).

List an automation's runs, newest first, phones masked: each with who it is for, its status (running, waiting, completed, stopped, failed) and why, and where it is. Filter `status` by a status or `tests`.

One run's log: its status, what started it (the order, the cart, the campaign), what it waits for and until when (`waiting`: kind wait, reply or held, and `at`), each line the engine wrote with its message's delivery status, and `next` while it runs or waits.
Cancel a campaign for good: whoever has not got it yet never will (they are skipped). Answers the campaign, cancelled.
endpoints.description: Only a scheduled, sending or paused campaign is cancelled: a draft answers 409 `campaign_is_draft` (delete it with campaigns.campaigns.delete) and a finished one 409 `campaign_ended`, both before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: Save a new campaign draft (name, audience, template, mapping, schedule): nothing is checked beyond its shape and nothing is sent. Answers the draft; then read campaigns.campaigns.estimate and schedule it with campaigns.campaigns.schedule.
endpoints.description: audience: {kind: segment, segment: all|…} or {kind: tags, any: [tags], none: [tags]}; only subscribed contacts are sent to. template_name and template_language: from campaigns.templates.list. mapping: {body: {"1": {source: name|fixed|…, value, fallback}}, header, buttons}. send_mode: now or later, with date (YYYY-MM-DD) and time (HH:MM) in Riyadh time. `intent` is ignored here: scheduling is campaigns.campaigns.schedule.

endpoints.summary: Delete a draft (nothing was ever sent from it); answers ok. A scheduled or sent campaign is cancelled instead (campaigns.campaigns.cancel): 409 not_draft.
Copy a campaign into a new draft with the same audience, template, mapping and image; answers the new draft.

A saved campaign's estimate, nothing sent: who it reaches and who is left out (and why), Meta's cost, Tawked's fee and the wallet's shortfall (for who may see the money), when it would start (moved out of the quiet hours), and what is still missing.

List the application's WhatsApp campaigns, newest first, each with its status, audience, template, when it sends and its figures (sent, delivered, read, replied, unsubscribed, failed). Filter by `status`.
Pause a scheduled or sending campaign: nobody else gets it until it is resumed. Answers the campaign.
The estimate of a campaign form not saved yet (the same fields as create), nothing written: reach, exclusions, cost, start time and what is missing.
Resume a paused campaign: sending goes on from where it stopped (within the quiet hours and the wallet). Answers the campaign.
endpoints.description: This messages customers again. Errors, each answered before any approval is asked: not_paused, insufficient_balance (the fee of who is still queued), template_unusable, mapping_incomplete, stops_unavailable, whatsapp_not_connected, whatsapp_blocked.

endpoints.summary: Schedule a draft to send: everything is checked, its recipients fixed (subscribed contacts, minus who stopped or already got the day's marketing message), its start moved out of the quiet hours; one due now starts at once. Answers the campaign, scheduled or sending, and `next`: read campaigns.campaigns.show every few minutes for its results.
endpoints.description: This messages customers. Every refusal below is answered before any approval is asked. Read campaigns.campaigns.estimate first. Errors (each its own code): not_draft, audience_missing, unknown_tags, audience_empty, template_unusable (with `template`: why), mapping_incomplete, image_missing, invalid_time, insufficient_balance, whatsapp_not_connected, whatsapp_blocked, meta_unavailable, stops_unavailable. Pause, resume or cancel it after.

endpoints.summary: Send the campaign's template with its mapping to your own Saudi mobile (the token's person), as a test: not a recipient, no Tawked fee, not the day's marketing message (Meta bills the message). Answers ok; then campaigns.campaigns.estimate and campaigns.campaigns.schedule.
endpoints.description: The same fields as create (template_name, template_language, mapping, header_image_path), and `campaign`: the draft it is for. At most 5 tests in 10 minutes. Errors: no_phone, template_unusable, mapping_incomplete (these three answered before any approval is asked), image_missing, meta_unavailable, send_failed.

endpoints.summary: One campaign: a draft as written (audience, template, mapping, image, schedule), or a scheduled or sent one with its results: the funnel (recipients, sent, delivered, read, replied, unsubscribed, failed, skipped, queued), why some failed or were skipped, the buttons tapped; and `next` from its status (none once completed or cancelled).
Replace a draft's fields (the whole form, as on create); answers the draft. Only a draft changes: 409 not_draft once it is scheduled.
Upload the image of a template that opens with one (a JPG or PNG up to 5 MB, multipart `image`); answers its `path`, to save on the draft as `header_image_path`, and its public URL.

List a scheduled or sent campaign's recipients in the order it reached them, phones masked: each with its status (queued, skipped, failed, sent, delivered, read), why, and the button tapped. Filters: status (delivered, read, replied, failed), q (a name or a whole Saudi mobile).
List the number's marketing templates as a campaign may use them: each with its label, language, placeholders to map and, when it cannot be picked, why (`reason`: pending, no_stop…).
endpoints.description: A campaign sends an approved MARKETING template that tells the customer how to stop (a footer or a quick reply). Create one in the whatsapp area, wait for Meta's approval, then pick it here.

endpoints.summary: The auto-attendant's log: every conversation it held, newest first, with the customer's name, the choices they tapped and how it ended (`answered`, `team`, `radeef`, `human`, `expired`, `stopped`, or `ongoing`).
endpoints.description: Search by name with `q` (and by phone for who manages the contacts, who alone read full numbers and the collected detail); narrow by `outcome` (`ended` is expired or stopped). Kept 90 days.

endpoints.summary: Publish the stored draft (the starter when nothing was saved yet) as the next live version of the auto-attendant: once it is on, customers get this menu. Answers the attendant.
endpoints.description: Refused while a problem stands, before any approval is asked: 422 `attendant_has_problems` with the `problems`. Publishing does not switch it on (chat.attendant.switch).

endpoints.summary: Save the auto-attendant's draft (`definition`, the whole menu): it reaches no customer. Answers when it was saved and the problems that keep it from being published.
endpoints.description: A draft saves with its problems; only a body that is not a definition at all is refused (422 `validation_failed` on `definition`: `not_object`, `too_large`, `bad_choice`, `too_many_choices`). Up to 64 KB and 256 choices.

endpoints.summary: The auto-attendant of this application's number: its state and whether it is on, its settings, the draft with the problems that keep it from being published, the published version, the people a fallback may go to, and the limits.
endpoints.description: Before the first save the draft is a starter menu, stored nowhere. The usual loop: chat.attendant.save_draft until `problems` is empty, chat.attendant.publish, then chat.attendant.switch with enabled=true. A definition is {version: 1, opening, list_button, away, fallback, choices: [{id: "c_…", title, description, action: {type: reply|submenu|ask|team|radeef, …}}]}; read the draft here for the exact shape. The menu needs at least one `team` choice.

endpoints.summary: Turn the auto-attendant on (`enabled: true`: it answers every new conversation on the number with the published menu) or off (its conversations go to the team). Answers the attendant.
endpoints.description: Errors: 409 `attendant_unpublished` (publish first), 409 `attendant_locked` (no number, Tawked Chat not on the number, or the number cannot send: see `state` and `lock` in chat.attendant.show), both answered before any approval is asked; 503 `chat_unavailable` (Tawked Chat did not answer; nothing changed).

endpoints.summary: Change the auto-attendant's settings: `mode` (`menu_then_radeef` or `menu_only`), the customers' `language` (`ar` or `en`), and who gets a fallback handoff (`fallback_assign`: `auto` or `member` with `fallback_member_id`, one of `assignees`). Answers the attendant and the settings before.

Check a link before adding it as a menu: whether Tawked Chat can open it inside the conversation (`frame`: `opens`, `window` or `unknown`), and the link's own problem if any (`problem`: `length`, `http`, `host`, or null).
endpoints.description: Advisory: a link that opens in a new window can still be a menu. The link may carry the tokens {customer_phone}, {customer_name}, {customer_email} and {conversation_id}, filled in for each conversation.

endpoints.summary: Add a chat menu: a page of your business (`title`, an https `url`) shown beside this application's conversations in Tawked Chat; `icon_mode` takes the site's icon (`site`, the default), an uploaded `icon` (`upload`) or none. Answers the menu.
endpoints.description: Errors: 422 `validation_failed` on `title` (`required`, `length`, `taken`), `url` (`required`, `http`, `host`, `length`, `reserved`) or `icon` (`type`, `small`); 409 `menu_limit_reached`, 409 `chat_not_ready` (the account has no Tawked Chat yet), 409 `number_not_in_chat` (this application's number is not in Tawked Chat yet); 503 `chat_unavailable` (nothing was kept).

endpoints.summary: Remove a chat menu from Tawked Chat and from this application; answers ok.
List the chat menus that show beside this application's conversations in Tawked Chat (its own, the ones of every conversation, and the Salla store's orders tab), in Tawked Chat's order.
endpoints.description: Up to 10 menus per application (the Salla tab and the ones of every conversation not counted). The whole link is shown only to who manages the menus. Every menu in one answer (no paging).

endpoints.summary: One chat menu of this application: its title, link, icon and whether it opens inside Tawked Chat.
Change a chat menu: send its `title` and `url` (both, as they should be), and `icon_mode` only to change the icon. Answers the menu.
endpoints.description: The same errors as chat.menus.create.

endpoints.summary: Where a person opens this application's conversations in Tawked Chat: the web address (they sign in with their own mobile), the phone apps once listed, the inbox's state, and whether this token's person answers this number's conversations.
endpoints.description: Give the person `web_url`. The console's own "Open Tawked Chat" button is a single-use sign-in for whoever presses it and is not offered here.

endpoints.summary: Add a person to this application's support team: someone of the account by `member_id`, or someone new by `name` with a `phone` (a Saudi mobile, 05… or +9665…), an `email`, or both, and a `role` (`agent` or `administrator`). Someone new with an email signs in with it and Tawked e-mails them the invitation (`invitation_sent_to`); with a mobile, answers `sign_in_message` for whoever added them to send, written in your person's language or `language` (ar or en).
endpoints.description: `member.provisioned` is false until the person first signs in to Tawked Chat (their Tawked Chat user is made then): nothing for you to do about it. Relay `human_action` to whoever added them: its link opens their own WhatsApp with `sign_in_message.text` written, to send; the person signs in to Tawked Chat with their own mobile, or with their email (`invitation_sent_to` names where Tawked e-mailed the invitation; resend it with chat.team.invite). `agent` answers this number's conversations; `administrator` (a supervisor) answers every number's and runs Tawked Chat. Errors: 422 `validation_failed` with `contact_required` (neither a mobile nor an email), 409 `phone_taken` (the mobile is another account's or Tawked's team's), 409 `email_taken` (the email is another account's, or another person's than the mobile's), 409 `already_on_team`, 409 `member_limit_reached` (no seat left: add a candidate instead), 403 `self_edit`, 403 `above_own_role` (each answered before any approval is asked), 503 `chat_unavailable` (Tawked Chat did not answer; nothing was written).

endpoints.summary: Who could join this support team without a new seat (the account's people not on it yet, mobiles masked), and the account's seats: the limit, how many are used, how many are left.
endpoints.description: Add one of them with chat.team.add and `member_id`. Someone new (by name and mobile) takes a seat: when `seats.left` is 0, only a candidate can join.

endpoints.summary: E-mail the invitation again to a person of this support team who signs in with an email: one a minute and five a day per person, the one sent at the add included. Answers ok.
endpoints.description: For someone added with an email (chat.team.add's `invitation_sent_to`). Errors: 409 `no_email` (the person signs in with a mobile), 429 `invite_wait`, 403 `self_edit`, 403 `above_own_role`.

endpoints.summary: List who answers this application's customers in Tawked Chat: the owner, the supervisors, then the agents of this number, each with their role, mobile (never the owner's) and whether you may change them.
endpoints.description: For who manages the support team (else 403). To add someone, read chat.team.candidates first: the account's people who are not here yet join without a new seat.

endpoints.summary: Take a person off this application's support team: an agent loses this number's conversations and keeps the others; a supervisor leaves Tawked Chat as a whole. Someone left with no role at all is removed from the account. Answers ok.
endpoints.description: Errors: 403 `self_edit`, 403 `above_own_role`, 503 `chat_unavailable` (nothing was written).

endpoints.summary: One person of this support team: their role, mobile, last sign-in, and what they are beyond this number (the other inboxes they answer, their console role).
Change a support team person's name and role (`agent` or `administrator`); the mobile never changes (it is how they sign in). Answers the person.
endpoints.description: A supervisor made an agent keeps this number's inbox and no other. Errors: 403 `self_edit`, 403 `above_own_role`, 503 `chat_unavailable` (nothing was written).

endpoints.summary: Read the Partner API's state: whether a partner key works (its prefix, expiry and allowlist; never the key), the sandbox key's prefix, the webhook (URL, events, threshold), its health and the newest deliveries.
endpoints.description: `webhook.threshold_halalas` is null for who may not see the money, `sandbox_destination` for who does not manage the clients.

endpoints.summary: Make a new partner key (tk_partner_…) for the Partner API; the key that worked until now stops at once. Answers the key's plaintext this once, with its prefix and the prefix of the key it replaced.
endpoints.description: Optional `expires_in_days` (30, 90, 180 or 365) and `ip_allowlist` (IP addresses or CIDR ranges separated by spaces or commas). Store the plaintext now: Tawked keeps only its hash.

endpoints.summary: Appeal Tawked's rejection of a client application with a note and an optional document (PDF or image, multipart); it goes back to Tawked's review. Your client is never told.
endpoints.description: Only while `appeal.state` is `available` on clients.applications.show; otherwise 409 `appeal_<state>` (open, declined, expired, not_appealable, blocked, none). Limited to 10 appeals in 10 minutes.

endpoints.summary: Approve a client application that waits on your decision (state awaiting_partner); it starts sending codes. Answers the application.
endpoints.description: 403 `not_allowed` when your approval mode leaves this one to Tawked; 409 `not_awaiting_decision` when it does not wait on you (read its state: a disabled or paused one is enabled or resumed first), `application_archived`; each answered before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: Archive a client application: it stops sending codes, leaves the lists and takes no write but clients.applications.restore. Answers the application.
endpoints.description: 409 `number_connected` while a WhatsApp number is connected to it, before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: Approve at once every listed client application that waits on your decision and whose names were screened clean; answers how many were approved and skipped.
endpoints.description: Body: `ids`, up to 500 application ids. A flagged name is never approved in bulk (decide it alone with clients.applications.approve); one that no longer waits on you is skipped.

endpoints.summary: Check the names of a client application before creating it: answers the screening's verdict and who would decide it (you, Tawked, or nobody: approved at once). Nothing is written.
endpoints.description: Body: `name_ar` and `name_en`, the names its users will read in the code's message. Limited to 60 checks a minute.

endpoints.summary: Open a Verify application for one of your clients (Verify only, Verify's default settings); answers it with its state: active at once, or awaiting a review by you or by Tawked, by your approval mode and the name's screening; `next` says what follows.
endpoints.description: `external_id` is your own id for the client: sending one that already exists answers that application (200, `created: false`) and changes nothing. Call clients.applications.check_name first to see the verdict the names would get. 403 `partner_suspended` while Tawked has suspended the partner.

endpoints.summary: Turn a client application off: no code goes out for it until clients.applications.enable. Answers the application.
Turn a client application you turned off back on; it sends codes again once nothing else holds it (its `state_detail.then`). Answers the application.

List the client applications this partner opened for its clients, each with its one state (active, awaiting_partner, awaiting_tawked, rejected, paused, suspended, disabled, archived), its codes and cost of the period.
endpoints.description: Filters: `q` (name, your external id or website), `state` (a pill: needs_you, active, review, rejected, stopped, disabled), `archived=1` to include archived ones, `sort` (newest, codes, waiting), `period` (the window the codes count, default 30d). The cost is null for who may not see the money.

endpoints.summary: Reject a client application that waits on your decision, with the reason; it sends no code. Answers the application.
endpoints.description: Body: `reason` (up to 500 characters). The same refusals as clients.applications.approve.

endpoints.summary: Restore an archived client application to where it stood before; answers the application.

Read one client application: its state and what it waits on, the code message its users read, its Verify settings, the last 30 days of usage, recent codes, its history, Tawked's rejection and its appeal, and what you may do on it (`can`).
Lift the pause Tawked's pumping guard put on a client application (state paused); answers the application.
Change a client application's names, website and industry; a change of what its users read sends it back to review. Answers the application with `review: true` when it went back to review.
endpoints.description: Send `name_ar`, `name_en` and `website_url` together (`industry` is optional and never sends it to review). 409 `application_archived` (restore it first) or `under_appeal` (Tawked is reading its appeal).

endpoints.summary: List the webhook's deliveries, newest first: each with its event, status (pending, delivered, failed), attempts, last answer, payload and the client application it was about.
endpoints.description: Filters: `status` (failed, pending, delivered) and `event`. Read the webhook's health with clients.webhook.health.

endpoints.summary: Send one failed delivery again, now; answers whether it was queued (a delivery that did not fail is left as it is).
Send every failed delivery again, one more attempt each; answers how many were queued (0 when none had failed).
endpoints.description: 409 `no_webhook` when no webhook URL is set.

endpoints.summary: Read the Clients place at a glance: your approval mode, what waits on you (the oldest five, with the count, and how many wait at Tawked), and the period's figures (active client applications, codes sent, verified rate, cost).
endpoints.description: `period`: 7d, 30d (default) or 90d. The cost and the price per code are null for who may not see the money.

endpoints.summary: List the client applications in review, oldest first: `queue=yours` (default) what waits on your decision, `queue=tawked` what waits at Tawked; each with since when it waits, its screening flags and whether you may approve it in bulk.
endpoints.description: Decide one with clients.applications.approve or clients.applications.reject, or several clean ones with clients.applications.bulk_approve. `q` searches the name or your external id.

endpoints.summary: Make a new sandbox key (tk_partner_test_…) for trying the Partner API without spending; the sandbox key before it stops at once. Answers its plaintext this once.

Read the usage you bill your clients from: per client application the codes sent, the codes verified and (for who may see the money) the Verify cost, busiest first, with the totals and your price per code.
endpoints.description: Period: `month` (YYYY-MM, this Riyadh month or one of the two before; default this one) or a custom `from`/`to` (YYYY-MM-DD, whole Riyadh days). `q` narrows the rows. The answer is one page of rows (`rows`, `next_cursor`), the totals of every row and the period.

endpoints.summary: Change some of a client application's Verify settings (a partial patch: only the fields sent change); answers the application with its settings.
endpoints.description: Fields: `code_length`, `ttl_seconds`, `max_attempts`, `max_per_hour`, `max_per_ip_per_hour`, `max_new_destinations_per_hour`, `autofill_domain_enabled` (boolean), `android_app_hash` (null clears it), `daily_spend_cap_halalas` (money: only who manages the wallet; null clears it). A value out of its bounds is 422 `validation_failed` naming the field; read the bounds in the console's settings page. 409 `application_archived`.

endpoints.summary: Read where the webhook stands (none, idle, delivering, failing), since when it fails, what waits, the last answer and the next automatic attempt, with the deliveries counted by status.
Answer the webhook's current signing secret (`secret`), to verify the deliveries' signatures; each reveal is recorded on the account.
Make a new signing secret for the webhook; the old one stops signing at once. Answers the secret this once.
Set the Partner API's webhook: its URL (empty turns it off), the events it receives and the balance.low threshold; answers the webhook as it stands.
endpoints.description: `url` must be a public https address. `events`: a list of the events clients.api.show names in `webhook.available_events` (omit to keep them). `threshold_sar` (SAR, decimals allowed) changes only for who may see the money. The signing secret is clients.webhook.rotate_secret or clients.webhook.reveal_secret.

endpoints.summary: Delete a contact for the business (its customer's data, PDPL): gone from the list now, its automations' runs stopped, forgotten for good 30 days later. Answers ok with `purge_at`, when it is forgotten.

List the application's WhatsApp contacts, newest first, phones masked: each with its consent status (subscribed, none, unsubscribed), tags and source. Filters: q (a name, or a whole Saudi mobile), status, tag, source.
endpoints.description: Only subscribed contacts receive campaigns. A phone's last digits search the list only for who manages the contacts. Read one contact for its whole phone (who manages the contacts) and its consent history.

endpoints.summary: Record that the customer agreed to receive marketing outside the opt-in link and an import (in person, in writing, on a call): subscribes them, with your note and your name as the evidence.
endpoints.description: method: in_person, written, phone_call or other; note: 3 to 500 characters saying how they agreed; attested: true (you confirm they agreed). The consent ledger is append-only: this line stays in the contact's history. It is the one way besides the customer's own word to subscribe someone who stopped.

endpoints.summary: One contact: its consent status from the ledger, tags, language, city, source, and its consent history newest first (who recorded each opt-in or stop, and the evidence).
Set a contact's tags to exactly this list (up to 10): missing tags are made, tags left on no contact are removed. Answers the contact and what was added and removed.
endpoints.description: Send the whole list (`tags: []` removes them all). A tag added may start the automations that are on with the trigger `contact.tagged`, which message this customer. An application holds at most 100 tags: beyond it, 409 too_many_tags.

endpoints.summary: Stop a contact's marketing messages (the customer asked you directly): recorded at once in the consent ledger; answers the contact, now unsubscribed. Nothing is recorded when they already are.
Confirm a pending import with how these people agreed to marketing; it runs in the background. Answers the import, `queued`, and `next`: poll contacts.imports.show until `status` is done or failed.
endpoints.description: basis: checkout (they ticked a box at checkout), form (a sign-up form) or none (no consent: added unsubscribed, they get no campaign). With checkout or form: consent_text (the words they agreed to, 10 to 1000 characters), consent_since (YYYY-MM-DD, not in the future) and attested: true (you confirm it); the contacts become subscribed, recorded in the consent ledger with this as the evidence. A contact who stopped stays unsubscribed. Confirming twice queues nothing more.

endpoints.summary: Upload a CSV of contacts (columns: phone, and optionally name, tags, city): read and counted, nothing imported yet. Answers the import, `pending`, with its preview (rows, valid, duplicates, outside Saudi Arabia, invalid); confirm it next with contacts.imports.confirm.
endpoints.description: Send the file as multipart `file`, or its text as `csv` in a JSON body (with an optional `file_name`). Tags in one cell are separated by commas. One import waits per person and application: a new file replaces the one not confirmed. Errors: 422 import_refused with `reason` (empty, encoding, no_phone_column, too_many_rows, type).

endpoints.summary: List the application's contact imports, newest first, each with its status, counts and outcome.
One import: its status (pending, queued, running, done, failed), its preview, its progress (`processed` of `total`), once done its result counted by outcome, and `next` until it is done.
The opt-in link: the wa.me link with its word, the welcome reply, whether it is on, and its QR code as SVG. Customers who send the word subscribe to marketing.
endpoints.description: `enabled` is false until the settings are saved once (until then the word subscribes nobody). `closed` true: stop replies cannot reach Tawked right now, so no link is given and the settings cannot change.

endpoints.summary: Set the opt-in link's word and its welcome reply; the first save turns the link on. Answers the link as it now stands.
endpoints.description: keyword: up to 30 characters, never a stop word nor a common word; welcome_reply: 10 to 500 characters. 409 opt_in_closed while stop replies cannot reach Tawked.

endpoints.summary: List the application's contact tags by name, each with how many live contacts carry it. Use a tag in a campaign's audience (`audience.kind: tags`).

Ask Tawked's team for early access to Tawked Email (its volume, an optional domain and note, the transactional-only promise); turns the product on for the application when it was off. Answers the access state, `pending` until the team decides, with `next`: read email.access.show every few hours until it is granted.
endpoints.description: Refusals: 409 `access_pending` (a request already waits), 409 `access_granted` (already granted), 429 `rate_limited`. `transactional_only` must be true: transactional is the one type of e-mail Tawked Email sends, marketing is not available.

endpoints.summary: Where Tawked Email stands on this application: whether the product is on, the account's early access (`none`, `pending`, `granted`, `declined`, `open`) with its latest request, the stage (`locked`, `setup`, `live`), the sending state, a pause and today's limit. Call it first.
endpoints.description: Until `granted` is true every other email operation answers 409 `email_access_required` (ask with `email.access.request`) or `email_access_pending` (Tawked's team decides: read this again every few hours). Once granted: `email.senders.create` to add a domain. `next` names the step for the stage it stands at, and is absent once e-mail sends.

endpoints.summary: Read the address's MX record now (as the console's Check now button does); answers the address with its state and `next`. Poll it every few minutes after adding the record until `state` is active.
endpoints.description: At most 6 checks an application a minute, the console's included (429 `inbound_check_rate`).

endpoints.summary: Remove a receiving address: email sent to it is refused from then on; its received emails stay until their 30 days end. Answers ok.
endpoints.description: A Tawked address's name is never given to another application; this application may take it again.

endpoints.summary: The application's receiving addresses: each one's kind (`hosted`, a Tawked address ready at once; `domain`, on a verified sending domain), its domain (every local part at it reaches the application, e.g. orders@ and support@), its state, its hold, today's count and where it forwards.
One receiving address: its state, the MX record to add for an address on your domain (`record`), the other MX hosts found, its hold, spam policy, automatic forward, test message and `next`.
endpoints.description: Reads the stored state: email.inbound.addresses.check reads the MX record again first.

endpoints.summary: Create a receiving address: `kind` hosted (a Tawked address, `slug` optional: `<slug>.inbound.tawked.com`, ready at once) or domain (`domain_id` a verified sending domain, `label` optional, default inbound: one MX record to add). Answers the address and `next`.
endpoints.description: One Tawked address per application and one address per verified domain (Tawked's limits). Each refusal but `inbound_label_taken` and `inbound_capacity` is answered before any approval is asked. Refusals: 409 `inbound_hosted_exists`, `inbound_slug_taken`, `inbound_address_exists`, `inbound_label_taken` (with `taken_by`), `inbound_domain_not_verified`, `inbound_custom_unavailable` (addresses on your own domain are not open yet); 422 `inbound_slug_invalid`, `inbound_label_invalid`; 503 `inbound_capacity`.

endpoints.summary: Send a free test email from Tawked to the address, to walk the whole path (the MX record, the receiving, the webhook); it shows in email.received.index within a minute. Answers ok and `next`.
endpoints.description: At most 6 in 10 minutes an application (429 `inbound_test_rate`).

endpoints.summary: Change one thing of a receiving address: `state` on or off, `spam_policy` keep or drop, or its automatic forward (`forward_to` one of your confirmed addresses or any address on a verified domain of the application, `forward_from_local`; `forward_to` null stops it). Answers the address.
endpoints.description: Send one of `state`, `spam_policy` or `forward_to` a call; its refusals are answered before any approval is asked. An automatic forward sends a copy of every email that is not spam from your domain, each a sent email, charged. Refusals: 422 `inbound_forward_not_allowed` (not a confirmed address nor on a verified domain), 409 `inbound_domain_not_verified` (turning on an address whose domain is not verified).

endpoints.summary: Make an application key for Tawked Email: `access` `send` (default: `email:send`, send e-mail and read what it sent) or `manage` (`email:manage`: also the domains, the suppression list and the templates on `/v1`), optionally limited to one domain (`domain_id`, sending keys only), `mode` `live` (default) or `test` (sends only to the simulator addresses, nothing delivered, nothing charged); answers the key once, with its id and prefix.
endpoints.description: The plaintext `key` is answered once and never again: hand it to the server's secret store. 409 `application_not_live` for a rejected or suspended application (a live key). 422 `key_domain_invalid` when `domain_id` is not one of the application's domains or the key is a test key, `key_domain_needs_sending_only` when a limited key would also manage; 422 `validation_failed` for an unknown `access` or `mode`, or a test key that would manage (`fields`). A full-access key never manages: `manage` is granted only here or in the console, by name.

endpoints.summary: Take back the pending request for a higher daily limit; answers the limit page.
endpoints.description: 409 `limit_request_none` when nothing waits, `limit_request_decided` once the team decided.

endpoints.summary: Ask Tawked's team for a higher daily e-mail limit (`requested_limit`, one of the offered choices up to the maximum; a note); answers the limit page with the request `pending` and `next`: read email.limit.show every few hours until the team answers.
endpoints.description: Refusals: 422 `limit_not_higher`, `limit_too_high`; 409 `limit_request_pending`, `limit_request_paused`, `limit_request_cooldown`, `limit_request_not_granted` (read `blocked` on `email.limit.show`).

endpoints.summary: The account's daily e-mail limit: today's use against it (each recipient counts), the requests a second (`per_second`; `per_minute` is the same rate a minute), when it resets, whether it refused a send today; this month's free e-mails (`free_allowance`) and the price after them (`price`); the higher limits one may ask for; the latest request with the team's answer; and why a request is not open now (`blocked`, `available_from`).
endpoints.description: `free_allowance`: `used` of `total` free e-mails this Riyadh month, `open` once the account has paid its first top-up (before that every e-mail is paid), `resets_at` the next month's start. `price`: `unit_halalas` a recipient after the allowance (a decimal string), `per_thousand_sar`.

endpoints.summary: Cancel a scheduled e-mail before its time: it is never sent and what it cost returns to the balance (the month's free e-mails too); answers the message, its `state` then `canceled`.
endpoints.description: Only while `state` is `scheduled`: else 409 `message_not_scheduled` (with `state` and the stored `status`). Another application's message answers 404. A new time is set through the public API (PATCH /v1/email/messages/{id}), not here.

endpoints.summary: The application's e-mail, newest first: each message's first recipient and how many more (`recipients`, `more`), subject, reference, state (`delivered`, `sent` for on its way, `scheduled`, `canceled`, `bounced`, `failed`), whether it was complained about, whether it was a test, its domain.
endpoints.description: Filters: `q` (an address of any recipient, a subject or a reference), `status` (`delivered`, `sent` for on its way, `scheduled`, `undelivered` for bounced or failed, `complained`; a canceled message shows with no filter only), `domain` (a domain id). Paged by `limit` and `cursor`. Messages are kept 30 days. 409 `email_locked` (with `locked.reason`: `product`, `access` or `domain`) before the log can hold anything.

endpoints.summary: The copy kept of one e-mail: its `subject`, `html` and `text` as sent (a template's rendered output), and `kept_until`. Only when the application keeps previews (email.settings.update) and kept this message.
endpoints.description: 404 `content_not_kept` when no copy is kept (previews off, or the message older than the switch). Every read is recorded on the account. The HTML is the sender's own: show it only in a sandbox that runs no script.

endpoints.summary: One e-mail: its row, the from and reply-to, each recipient with its type and own state (`recipients_list`), its tags, the custom headers' names, the time it waits for (`scheduled_at`), its attachments' names and sizes, each event in order (accepted, sent, delayed, delivered, bounced, complained, failed, canceled), the bounce (type, subtype, the receiving server's words) or the failure code, whether the address is now suppressed, the key that sent it, and the price for who sees the money.

The application's e-mail figures over Riyadh days: sent, delivered, delayed, bounced (permanent and transient), complained, failed, suppressed, opens and clicks, as totals, rates and one row per day, week (from Sunday) or month; answers `totals`, `rates` and `data`.
endpoints.description: Query: `from` and `to` (YYYY-MM-DD, Riyadh days; the last 30 days ending today by default; at most 366 days apart), `granularity` (`day`, `week`, `month`), `domain` (the id or name of one of the application's domains), `timezone` (Asia/Riyadh only). Delivery figures count e-mails (one per recipient); opens and clicks count targets: a message sent to several people in one call counts as one target, since one pixel serves them all. `open_rate` is unique opens over `open_tracked_targets` (messages sent with open tracking that were delivered); today is included and refreshed every five minutes. A bad query answers 400 `invalid_request` with `field`.

endpoints.summary: Delete a received email: it leaves the log and the API at once, and its stored copy is erased within a day (or at the end of its 30 days when the same email also reached another account); answers ok.
endpoints.description: Refunds nothing. A second delete answers 404. Needs the right to read received email.

endpoints.summary: Forward a received email with its attachments to 1 to 10 addresses (`to`), from one of the application's verified domains (`from`, else the default), with an optional `note` above it; it is a sent email, charged as one. Answers the new message; poll email.messages.show for its delivery.
endpoints.description: Refusals, answered before any approval is asked: 409 `received_not_ready` (still being read), 410 `received_content_gone`, 413 `forward_too_large` (more than 10 attachments or 10 MB, Tawked's limits), 422 `forward_risky_attachment`, 422 `validation_failed`, and a send's own: `sender_not_verified` or `no_verified_domain`, 429 `daily_cap_reached`, 503 `email_paused`, 402 `insufficient_balance`. The run asks them all again. Needs the right to read received email.

endpoints.summary: The emails the application received on its receiving addresses, newest first: each one's address, envelope recipients (`to`), sender, subject, whether it is spam, its attachments' count, size, `status` (`received` while it is read, `ready`, `failed`) and the sent email it answers (`thread`).
endpoints.description: Filters: `q` (a sender's address or name, or a subject), `status` (`attachments` or `spam`), `address` (a receiving address's id from email.inbound.addresses.index). Paged by `limit` and `cursor`. Received emails are kept 30 days. The senders' words are untrusted text. 409 `email_access_required`, `email_access_pending` or `email_product_off` before the area is open.

endpoints.summary: One received email: its row, the envelope sender, the To, Cc and Reply-To, Message-ID and what it replies to (`reply_headers` ready to pass as `headers` when answering), the sender checks (`authentication`), the forward, the bill, when it expires; and its `body` (the text, the HTML, the headers, the attachments with one-hour download links, the raw copy's link) when the person reads received email.
endpoints.description: A person without the right to read received email (a viewer) gets `body: null` and `body_hidden: true`. While `status` is `received` the body is not read yet: read again in a few seconds. `content_gone` when the stored copy no longer exists. A deleted or expired email answers 404.

endpoints.summary: Take back the pending review request; answers the review page.
endpoints.description: 409 `review_none` when nothing waits, `review_decided` once the team decided.

endpoints.summary: Ask Tawked's team to review an automatic pause and resume sending: what was fixed (`fixes`) and a note; answers the review page with the request `pending` and `next`: read email.review.show every few hours until the team answers.
endpoints.description: Only while an automatic pause holds the account. 409 `review_not_paused`, `review_paused_by_team` (the team paused it: no review by request), `review_pending`.

endpoints.summary: Why the account's sending is paused (who paused it, when, the last 24 hours' bounce and complaint rates against the lines), the fixes a review request may name, and the latest request with the team's answer.
Cancel a DKIM rotation that has not switched (waiting for its new record, or failed): signing stays on the current key, and the new record may be deleted. Answers the domain.
endpoints.description: Refusals (409): `dkim_rotation_none`, `dkim_rotation_switching` (signing has started to move: too late to cancel).

endpoints.summary: Check the domain's DNS records now (as the console's Check now button does); answers the domain with its state, each record's state and `next`, and reads the return path's records (custom MAIL FROM, SPF) and the DMARC record again into `authentication`. Poll it every one to two minutes after adding the records until `state` is verified; it is the one way to read DMARC anew.
endpoints.description: At most 6 checks an application a minute, the console's included (429 `rate_limited`). DNS can take minutes to spread: a `pending` answer is normal at first. 503 `email_unavailable` when the e-mail service cannot be read.

endpoints.summary: A link the person opens to add the domain's DNS record at their DNS host automatically (Domain Connect, e.g. Cloudflare): they sign in at the host and approve, then return to the domain's page in the console. Answers `url`, the `human_action` to relay and `next`: once the person says it is done, poll `email.senders.check`.
endpoints.description: Only where the domain's host supports Domain Connect (`connect_available` on the domain); otherwise 409 `connect_unavailable`, and the records are added by hand or with the host's own API. The link is the person's, for one trip.

endpoints.summary: Add a sending domain (e.g. shop.example.com) to the application; answers the domain with the DNS records to add at its DNS host and `next`. Add them (with the host's own tools or API), then poll `email.senders.check` every one to two minutes until `state` is `verified`.
endpoints.description: Adding a domain the application already has answers that domain. Before Tawked Email is open to the account, every senders operation answers 409 `email_access_required` (ask with email.access.request) or `email_access_pending` (Tawked's team decides: read email.access.show later), and 409 `email_product_off` once granted while the application's Email is off. Refusals: 422 `domain_invalid`, `domain_public` (a public mailbox's domain such as gmail.com), `domain_tawked`; 409 `domain_taken` (verified by another application), `domain_limit` (the application holds its most domains); 503 `email_unavailable`. A pending domain waits up to `pending_hours` for its records.

endpoints.summary: Remove a sender domain from the application: its sends stop at once (its messages stay in the log); answers ok.

The application's sender domains, newest first, each with its state (`pending`, `verified`, `failed`), the DNS records to add and their state, the DNS host when known, the default from address and the messages of the last 30 days.
Try a failed DKIM rotation again once its new record is in place at the DNS host: answers the domain with the rotation publishing again.
endpoints.description: Refusals (409): `dkim_rotation_none` (no rotation under way), `dkim_rotation_not_failed`, `dkim_rotation_retry_limit` (tried again its most times: cancel it and start a new one), `dkim_rotation_unavailable`.

endpoints.summary: Start rotating a verified domain's DKIM key: answers the domain with `authentication.dkim.rotation.new_record`, a second TXT record to add beside the current one. Tawked switches signing to it by itself once it reads it, then the old record is deleted at the DNS host (`old_record`).
endpoints.description: Poll email.senders.show every few minutes for `authentication.dkim.rotation.state` (publishing, switching, retiring, failed). Refusals (409): `dkim_rotation_unavailable` (not open yet: `authentication.rotation_available` is false), `domain_not_verified`, `dkim_rotation_active`, `dkim_rotation_needs_return_path` (the DMARC policy is quarantine or reject and the return path is not working: set it first with email.senders.set_mail_from).

endpoints.summary: Send a free test e-mail from a verified domain to one of the person's own confirmed addresses (`to`, one of `email.test_address.show`'s `recipients`); answers the message; poll `email.messages.show` for its delivery.
endpoints.description: Never to an address typed freely: with no confirmed address, confirm one first (`email.test_address.send_code`, `email.test_address.confirm`). Refusals: 409 `domain_not_verified`, 422 `recipient_not_allowed`, the send's own code (429 `test_limit_reached`, 422 `recipient_suppressed`, 503 `email_paused`), 503 `send_failed`. At most 6 in 10 minutes per person.

endpoints.summary: Name the domain's return path (custom MAIL FROM, `label` before the domain: `send` makes send.example.com) or turn it on again with its label; answers the domain with `authentication.mail_from` and its two records (an MX and an SPF TXT) to add at the DNS host. Optional: it makes SPF align with the domain and never affects verification or sending.
endpoints.description: Until both records are found the mail goes out with the default return path, so it never stops. The label is 1 to 63 of a-z, 0-9 and inner hyphens (422 `mail_from_label_invalid`); a name another service already uses (its own MX, a CNAME or an SPF record that is not Tawked's) is refused with 409 `mail_from_label_taken`. 503 `email_unavailable` when the e-mail service cannot be reached. A pending domain may have one.

endpoints.summary: One sender domain: its state, the DNS records to add at its host (name, value, the host's Name field, each record's state), how long a pending domain still waits, the default from address and its messages of the last 30 days, day by day; and its `authentication`: the DKIM key and its rotation (`dkim.rotation.state`), the return path (custom MAIL FROM, SPF alignment) with its records, the DMARC record and policy as last read, and the Feedback-IDs.
endpoints.description: Reads the stored state: email.senders.check reads DNS (the records, the return path and DMARC) again first.

endpoints.summary: Switch open and click tracking on or off for a verified sender domain (`opens`, `clicks`) and choose its tracking subdomain's label (`label`, `links` by default: links.<domain>); answers `tracking` (state `awaiting_dns`, `awaiting_tls`, `active` or `failing`, and the problem) and the one CNAME `record` to add.
endpoints.description: Turning it on waits for one CNAME, `<label>.<domain>` to Tawked's tracking edge: add it at the domain's DNS host, then poll `email.senders.check` every few minutes until `tracking.state` is `active`; from then on the domain's mail is tracked. Problems: `cname_missing`, `cname_elsewhere`, `proxied` (a proxied record, e.g. Cloudflare's orange cloud: make it DNS only), `tls_not_ready`, `edge_unreachable`, `ses_failed`. Refusals: 409 `domain_not_verified`, 409 `tracking_unavailable`, 422 `tracking_subdomain_invalid`, 409 `tracking_subdomain_taken` (the subdomain already has other records), 503 `email_unavailable`. Leave click tracking off on a domain that sends sign-in codes or password resets, or mark such links `data-tawked-track="off"`.

endpoints.summary: Turn the domain's return path off: its mail goes out with the default return path again (SPF no longer aligns with the domain); the label is kept for email.senders.set_mail_from. Answers the domain.
endpoints.description: 503 `email_unavailable` when the e-mail service cannot be reached.

endpoints.summary: Set a verified domain's defaults: the name a message is from (`from_name`, may be empty) and the part before the @ (`from_local`, e.g. no-reply) used when a send names no `from`; answers the domain.
The application's Email settings: `keep_previews`, whether a copy (subject, HTML, text) of each message sent from now on is kept for its 30 days, and when and by whom it last changed.

Turn on or off keeping a copy of each message (`keep_previews`); answers the settings. On, every message sent from then on keeps its subject, HTML and text for its 30 days, read with email.messages.preview; off, every copy is deleted at once.
endpoints.description: Body `{"keep_previews": true|false}`. Turning it off deletes every kept copy of the application's messages within minutes; the database's backups keep a deleted copy for up to their own retention (30 days, and 30 more for an older backup version). Needs the senders' permission (403 otherwise).

endpoints.summary: Put up to 1,000 addresses on the account's suppressed list, for this application: no application of the account sends e-mail to them; answers how many were added, already there, and which were not valid.
endpoints.description: Body `{ "addresses": ["a@example.sa", ...] }`, at most 1,000 (a Tawked limit). Each address is lower-cased; one already on the list is left as it is (`existing`). 201 `{ "added", "existing", "invalid": [{ "index", "code": "invalid_address" }] }` (`index` 0-based). 422 `suppression_invalid_addresses` when none is valid, `suppression_too_many` over 1,000. 409 `email_locked` before the list can hold anything. A CSV file is added from the console.

endpoints.summary: Lift an address off the suppressed list: e-mail can reach it again; a complaint needs a reason; answers ok.
endpoints.description: A bounce or a manual entry is lifted as it is. A complaint needs `reason`: `recipient_asked`, `reported_by_mistake` or `other` with a `note` of 10 to 500 characters (422 `suppression_lift_reason_required`); a complaint lifted once before and raised again is lifted only by Tawked's team (403 `suppression_team_only`). A row another application's message caused is lifted only by a person who sees every application, with a token for every application (403 otherwise; `reachable` on the list says which).

endpoints.summary: The addresses the account no longer sends e-mail to, newest first: why (`bounce`, `complaint`, `manual`), where from (`source`), since when, whether and how it may be lifted, and the message that caused it.
endpoints.description: The list is the account's (a send from any of its applications is refused to these). Filters: `q` (an address), `reason`. Paged by `limit` and `cursor`. 409 `email_locked` before the page can hold anything. A row another application's message caused names it only as `here: false` to a person or a token that does not reach every application. `source`: `event` (a bounce or complaint), `manual`, `import`, `api`, `ses` (adopted from the sending service). `lift_needs_reason`: a complaint, lifted with a reason; `team_only`: a complaint lifted once already, which only Tawked's team lifts. Add with email.suppressions.create, lift with email.suppressions.delete.

endpoints.summary: Create a hosted e-mail template (a draft; `publish: true` publishes it at once); answers the template with its problems; send by it with `template: {id or alias, variables}` on a message once published.
endpoints.description: Body `{ "name", "alias"?, "subject", "html"?, "text"?, "from"?: {"name","address"}, "reply_to"?: [..], "variables"?: [{"key","fallback"}], "publish"?: bool }`. Without `variables` they are the placeholders found, fallbacks null. A template: `id`, `alias`, `name`, `state` (`draft` never published, `published`, `published_with_draft`), `published_version` (its number), `published` and `draft` (each: `subject`, `html`, `text`, `from`, `reply_to`, `variables` [{key, fallback}], `placeholders`, `problems` [{code, key?, severity}]). The language: `{{ KEY }}` is the value, HTML-escaped in html; `{{{ KEY }}}` unescaped in html; no loops or conditions. Refusals: 400 `invalid_request` (`field`), 422 `template_alias_invalid`, 409 `template_alias_taken`, 409 `template_limit` (100, a Tawked limit), 422 `template_invalid` with `problems` when `publish` is true and the draft has an error.

endpoints.summary: Delete a hosted e-mail template: sends by its id or alias are refused from now on (422 template_not_found) and its alias is free again; answers ok.
The application's hosted e-mail templates, last changed first: each one's id, alias, name, state and its published and draft versions without their bodies; read one with email.templates.show.
endpoints.description: A template: `id`, `alias`, `name`, `state` (`draft` never published, `published`, `published_with_draft`), `published_version` (its number), `published` and `draft` (each: `subject`, `html`, `text`, `from`, `reply_to`, `variables` [{key, fallback}], `placeholders`, `problems` [{code, key?, severity}]). The language: `{{ KEY }}` is the value, HTML-escaped in html; `{{{ KEY }}}` unescaped in html; no loops or conditions. At most 100 templates an application (a Tawked limit), all answered at once.

endpoints.summary: Publish a template's draft as its next numbered version: sends by the template use it from now on; answers the template.
endpoints.description: 409 `template_no_draft` when no draft waits; 422 `template_invalid` with `problems` while the draft has an error (an undeclared placeholder, an empty subject, no html and no text, html over 512 KB, a from address off the application's domains).

endpoints.summary: Copy a published version of a template into its draft (the published version keeps sending until the draft is published); answers the template.
endpoints.description: 404 `not_found` for a number the template never published.

endpoints.summary: One hosted e-mail template by its id or alias, with its published version and its draft in full and each one's problems.
endpoints.description: A template: `id`, `alias`, `name`, `state` (`draft` never published, `published`, `published_with_draft`), `published_version` (its number), `published` and `draft` (each: `subject`, `html`, `text`, `from`, `reply_to`, `variables` [{key, fallback}], `placeholders`, `problems` [{code, key?, severity}]). The language: `{{ KEY }}` is the value, HTML-escaped in html; `{{{ KEY }}}` unescaped in html; no loops or conditions.

endpoints.summary: Send a template's draft (or its published version when no draft waits) as a free test to one of the person's own confirmed addresses; answers the message; poll email.messages.show for its delivery.
endpoints.description: Body `{ "to"?: one of email.test_address.show's `recipients` (the first when absent), "variables"?: {KEY: value} }`; a missing value takes its fallback. From the version's own address when it is on a verified domain, else the domain's default. Refusals: 409 `no_test_address` (confirm one with email.test_address.send_code), 422 `recipient_not_allowed`, 409 `domain_not_verified`, 422 `template_invalid` with `problems`, the variable codes (`template_variable_missing`, `template_variable_unknown`, `template_variable_invalid`, `template_variables_invalid`), and the send's own (429 `test_limit_reached`, 503 `email_paused`).

endpoints.summary: Change a template's name or alias, or its draft (made from the published version when none waits); the published version keeps sending until the draft is published; answers the template.
endpoints.description: The body of email.templates.create, every key optional; `publish: true` publishes the draft after the change. A template: `id`, `alias`, `name`, `state` (`draft` never published, `published`, `published_with_draft`), `published_version` (its number), `published` and `draft` (each: `subject`, `html`, `text`, `from`, `reply_to`, `variables` [{key, fallback}], `placeholders`, `problems` [{code, key?, severity}]). The language: `{{ KEY }}` is the value, HTML-escaped in html; `{{{ KEY }}}` unescaped in html; no loops or conditions.

endpoints.summary: A template's published versions, newest first: number, state (`published` or `superseded`), subject, when published; restore one into the draft with email.templates.restore.
Confirm the waiting address with the six-digit code the person received (`code`); it becomes the person's own confirmed e-mail and a test recipient. Answers the recipients.
endpoints.description: Refusals: 409 `nothing_pending` (send a code first, or it expired), 422 `code_invalid`, 429 `too_many_attempts` or `rate_limited`, 409 `email_taken`.

endpoints.summary: Drop the address waiting for its code (to type another); answers ok.
Send a six-digit code to an address the person owns (`email`), so it can receive test e-mails once confirmed; answers the address waiting for its code and when a new code may be asked for.
endpoints.description: The person reads the code in that mailbox: relay `human_action`, then give what they tell you to `email.test_address.confirm`. Refusals: 422 `invalid_address`, 409 `email_taken` (another person's confirmed e-mail), 429 `rate_limited`, `code_cooldown` or `daily_limit`, 503 `unavailable`.

endpoints.summary: The addresses a test e-mail may go to for this person (`recipients`: the account's notification e-mail, the person's confirmed e-mail, the account's confirmed business e-mail), and the address waiting for its code, if any.
endpoints.description: With no recipients, confirm an address the person owns: `email.test_address.send_code`, then `email.test_address.confirm` with the code they received.
