endpoints.summary: Make an integration app, in testing (open to this account's own applications only); answers it with its client id and its client secret, the secret this once.
endpoints.description: Fields: `name_ar`, `name_en` (never Tawked's name), `site_url` (https), `redirect_uris` (1 to 5 https return addresses), optional `connect_url`, `description` and `logo` (PNG or JPEG, multipart). 409 `limit_reached` past the account's limit (answered, like a name that is Tawked's, before any approval is asked). Store the secret now; clients see the app only once Tawked approves it (integration_apps.apps.submit).

endpoints.summary: Delete an integration app that was never approved, with its test connections (their keys revoked), its requests and its client. Cannot be undone.
endpoints.description: 409 `approved_not_deleted` for an approved app: clients depend on it.

endpoints.summary: List the integration apps this partner account made, newest first: each with its status (testing, in_review, approved, rejected), whether a change waits for Tawked's team, and how many applications it is connected to.

Read one integration app: its status, client id, facts, return addresses, the change that waits for Tawked's team, why it was sent back, what the review still needs (`checklist`) and what may be done now (`can`). Never its secret.

Send an integration app in testing (or sent back) to Tawked's review; answers it in_review. Tawked's team approves it or sends it back with a reason: `next` says how often to read integration_apps.apps.show.
endpoints.description: 409 `not_ready` while its `checklist` has a line not done (names, site, a return address, a description), `wrong_state`, `app_stopped`.

endpoints.summary: Replace an integration app's facts and return addresses; answers the app and `outcome`: saved (at once, while testing or sent back), proposed (approved: the reviewed facts wait for Tawked's team, the approved ones keep working), cancelled (the change that waited was dropped) or unchanged.
endpoints.description: The same fields as integration_apps.apps.create, all sent again, plus `remove_logo`. 409 `in_review` while it waits for the team (withdraw it first).

endpoints.summary: Take an integration app back from Tawked's review, to testing, so it can be edited; answers the app.
Drop the change of an approved integration app that waits for Tawked's team; the approved facts stay. Answers the app.
Renew an integration app's client secret: the old one stops at once, so the app's sign-ins fail until it uses the new one. Answers the new secret this once.
End a connected app's connection: its key stops at its next call; the templates it made stay the client's and the record is kept. Answers ok.
endpoints.description: The app must ask for access again, and someone who manages the application's keys approve it, to connect again.

endpoints.summary: List the apps connected to the application now: each connection's id, the app (name, host, logo), its state (connected, stopped) and when it was approved and last called.

Read one connected app's connection: who the app is, its state, what it may do, who approved it and when, and (for who reads Notifications) the messages it sent, the templates it made and its last calls.
Say (`attested: true`) or withdraw that the Larm store's checkout collects its customers' consent to marketing messages; answers the consent as it stands.
endpoints.description: A statement for the business, by the owner or an admin, recorded with who and when. Given, the cart reminder reaches every buyer who has not stopped marketing, not only those who opted in. Saying again what is said changes nothing. Refusals: 409 store_not_linked.

endpoints.summary: Disconnect the Larm store from the application: Tawked drops its tokens and its webhook subscription, the messages stop, and the record stays. Answers ok. The merchant connects it again by opening Tawked from Larm.
endpoints.description: For who manages the application's keys: the store's tokens are a credential, as a key is. Refusals: 409 store_not_linked when no active store is linked.

endpoints.summary: Switch one of the Larm store's messages on or off (`enabled`), or set which order statuses an order update speaks about (`statuses`: completed, cancelled, refunded, each true or false); answers whether it was on before.
endpoints.description: Kinds: order_confirmed, order_status, digital_delivery, abandoned_cart (the cart reminder is marketing: it reaches a buyer who did not stop marketing once the store attested its consent, express opt-ins alone before). Turning a message on sends WhatsApp messages to the store's buyers on each matching event and asks Meta for its template. `statuses` is read for order_status alone. Refusals: 404 for a kind the catalog lacks, 409 store_not_linked.

endpoints.summary: Read the Larm store linked to the application: the store (name, address, status, the permissions Larm granted, who linked it and when) and its four WhatsApp messages (order confirmed, order status with its three statuses, digital delivery, abandoned cart), each with its switch, its state and the week's count, with the checkout's consent. `store` is null when no Larm store was ever linked.
endpoints.description: A message's `state` says what it still needs: ready, no_number, scope_missing (with `missing_scopes`), template_missing, template_pending, template_rejected, suspended. `messages` is null while the store is not serving (disconnected, uninstalled). A Larm store connects from Larm's own app store, never from here: `next` says so when none is linked.

endpoints.summary: Read an application's integrations at a glance: its Salla or Zid store, a Larm store linked to it, Supabase phone sign-in (for who reads Verify), the WooCommerce plugin's state (none, waiting, connected) and the connected apps. Open each with its own operation.

Connect Supabase's Send SMS hook to this application (once; again answers the same connection): answers the hook URL and its secret, and the `human_action` that has the person paste them into Supabase › Auth › Hooks (only they reach their Supabase dashboard).
Disconnect Supabase: the hook stops sending codes at once and the keys it sent with are revoked; the codes it sent stay in the Verify log. Answers ok.
Replace the hook's secret: a new one made by Tawked (no body), or the one Supabase's hook settings generated (`secret`, `v1,whsec_…`); answers the hook URL and the secret, once.
endpoints.description: Supabase's hook fails its signature until it holds the same secret. A pasted value that is not a Standard Webhooks secret is 422 validation_failed.

endpoints.summary: Read the application's Supabase phone sign-in: how codes go out (live, review: the owner's phone only, blocked), the connection's hook URL, language, last call and outcome, and the last codes it sent.
endpoints.description: The hook's secret is not shown here: integrations.supabase.connect and integrations.supabase.secret answer it. `connection` is null until connected.

endpoints.summary: Run the hook as Supabase would for a sign-in on the account owner's own phone: a real code is sent there with the test key; answers the outcome, the hook's status and body, and the request it was given.
endpoints.description: Charges one code at the application's price. A test that sent nothing did not run: 402 `insufficient_credits` (with the `human_action` that tops the wallet up) and 422 `no_owner_phone` (no verified owner phone) are answered before any approval is asked, and by the run itself. Another refusal of the hook is an `outcome` (e.g. `not_active`, `sandbox_quota_exceeded`) with the hook's body. At most 10 every 10 minutes.

endpoints.summary: Set the language of the sign-in codes Supabase's hook sends (`lang`: ar or en); answers ok.
Disconnect the WooCommerce plugin: every key it holds is revoked and the store stops sending codes and order updates until it gets a new key. Answers how many keys were revoked.

Make the WooCommerce plugin's key (`mode`: live, or test while the application is in review); answers its plaintext once, and the `human_action` that has the person install the plugin and paste it into its settings. A key of that mode it held before is revoked.
endpoints.description: Refusals: 409 application_not_active (a live key before the application is approved), 409 test_key_in_review_only (a test key once it is live), 403 insufficient_permission when this token lacks `verify:write` or `whatsapp:write` that the plugin's key reaches.

endpoints.summary: Read where the WooCommerce plugin stands on the application: the plugin's version and download, the live and test keys it holds (prefix, last use), which key may be made now, its last call, what WhatsApp order updates need, its `state` (none, waiting, connected) and `next`.
Who this token acts for: the person, the account, the token's permissions, the applications it reaches with their products, and `next_steps`: what is left to set up. Call it first.
endpoints.description: `next_steps` lists, per application the token reaches, each product's setup guide that is not complete yet (as Home shows it): every step with `done`, `current` (the one to take now), `optional`, and `waiting` (Tawked's team, Meta or the customers move it, not you). An undone step carries the `operation` that does it (or, while it waits, the one that reads where it stands), or a `human_action` a person must take: tell them its `say` with its `url`, then call its `then` once they are done. `docs` is where a step done by the application's own integration is explained. An empty list means everything is set up.

endpoints.summary: Add a member by `name` and `phone` (a Saudi mobile, 05… or +9665…) with a console `role` and what they manage; answers the member and `sign_in`, the message to send them, written in your person's language or `language` (ar or en). Tawked sends nothing.
endpoints.description: role: viewer, developer or admin (never above your own). all_applications: true, or access: [{application_id, products: null for the whole application or a list}]. Relay `human_action` to the person who added them: its link opens their own WhatsApp with `sign_in.message` written, and they send it (Tawked sends nothing). Errors: phone_taken 409, invalid_phone 422, limit_reached 409, invalid_role / no_applications / invalid_application / no_products / invalid_product / invalid_clients_access 422; each answered before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: Remove a member from the console: their role and access go (and their saved cards); someone who also answers in Tawked Chat stays on their support teams (chat.team.remove takes them off). Answers ok.
endpoints.description: The owner and yourself cannot be removed (403), answered before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: List the account's people who manage on tawked.com (the owner first, then each member with their role and what they manage); `application` narrows to who manages that application.
endpoints.description: For the owner and the admins who see every application, as the console's Members page. Someone who only answers customers in Tawked Chat is not listed here (see the chat area's support team). For a token narrowed to some applications, each member's `access` and `support.applications` name only those applications.

endpoints.summary: One member: role, every application or the chosen ones with their products, Clients access on a partner account, last sign-in, and whether you may change them.
endpoints.description: For a token narrowed to some applications, `access` and `support.applications` name only those applications.

endpoints.summary: Change a member's name, e-mail, role and what they manage (the phone never changes: it is how they sign in); answers the member.
endpoints.description: Send the whole member as the console's form does: name, email, role, all_applications or access, and clients_access on a partner account. The owner and yourself cannot be changed (403); every refusal of the change is answered before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: Search the operations by words (`q`) and area (`area`); each with its method, path, summary, whether it is consequential, and `allowed`: whether this token may call it. When `allowed` is false, `needs` names the permission its person would add on the token's page. The best `limit` matches (default 50) in one answer.
endpoints.description: Operations this token cannot call are listed too, ranked with the rest, so you know they exist: calling one answers 403 `insufficient_permission` with a `human_action` that opens the token's page with that permission ready to allow.

endpoints.summary: One operation in full: its path parameters, the JSON Schema of its body (a write) or its query (a read), `allowed` (whether this token may call it) and `next` (how to call it). When `allowed` is false, `needs` names the permission and `human_action` opens the token's page with it ready to allow.
endpoints.description: An id no operation has answers 404 `not_found` with `did_you_mean`: up to 3 nearest operations, each with its id, method and path.

endpoints.summary: Read Radeef (the AI agent answering this application's WhatsApp customers): its state (setup, live, draft, off, paused_budget, paused_balance, locked, unavailable) and why, mode, name, hours mode, what it knows and this month's spend.
endpoints.description: `state` is the one truth: `live` answers customers, `draft` only suggests replies to the team, `locked` names its `lock` (`number`: connect a WhatsApp number with Chat on; `payment` or `blocked`: the number cannot send), `paused_budget` and `paused_balance` hand everything to the team until the cap or the wallet allows. `fix_url` is the console page a person opens to fix it.

endpoints.summary: Correct a reply Radeef sent a customer: the `question` in general terms (never the customer's words) and the right `answer` become an FAQ every customer gets from now on; answers the FAQ.
endpoints.description: Only a delivered reply Radeef wrote can be corrected (404 otherwise); a reply corrected again saves over its correction.

endpoints.summary: List Radeef's conversations with customers, newest first, ten a page: who, what they asked first, the outcome (resolved, handed_off, abandoned, ongoing) and the handoff's reason; filter by `outcome`, `reason`, `period` (today, 7d, 30d, month) and `q`.
endpoints.description: The full phone only for who manages contacts, masked otherwise. `next_cursor` is the next page's number. Texts are removed after the retention period.

endpoints.summary: Read one of Radeef's conversations: the customer, the outcome, and the transcript (the customer's messages, Radeef's replies with how each was made and the sources it used, its notes to the team, the handoff, the close).
endpoints.description: A reply with `correctable: true` is corrected with radeef.conversations.correct (its `turn_id`).

endpoints.summary: Add an FAQ Radeef answers from (`question`, `answer`); answers the source. Check it with radeef.playground.send.
endpoints.description: 422 `faqs_full` past 300 FAQs.

endpoints.summary: Delete an FAQ (or a correction) from what Radeef knows; answers ok.
Correct an FAQ (or a correction) Radeef answers from: its `question` and `answer`; answers the source.
Save a file's text (`content`, corrected or as extracted) and approve it, so Radeef reads it from now on; answers the source.
endpoints.description: 422 `file_reading` while its text is still being extracted. A file whose reading failed takes the text pasted from its source here.

endpoints.summary: Upload a file for Radeef (multipart `file`: PDF, DOCX, TXT or MD, up to 5 MB); its text is extracted in the background, then waits for approval: answers the file, `state` reading, then review (radeef.files.show, radeef.files.approve).
endpoints.description: Send it as multipart/form-data. 422 `files_full` past 10 files. Radeef never reads a file before its text is approved.

endpoints.summary: Delete a file, its text and what Radeef read from it; answers ok.
Read a file of Radeef's with its review: its state, the extracted text to correct and approve, whether its Arabic reads reversed.
Read the team's week as Radeef reads it from the Tawked Chat inbox (or the suggestion when it holds none), its timezone, and Radeef's hours mode and Ramadan schedule.
endpoints.description: Change the week with radeef.settings.update, section `hours`, field `week`.

endpoints.summary: Read what Radeef did in a `period` (today, 7d, 30d, month): conversations resolved and handed off against the period before, by the hour they started, and why it handed over, most common first.

Read what Radeef knows in counts (pages, confirmed facts, FAQs, files, corrections, products), each topic's state, the sources used most in 30 days, and what it noticed (pages to confirm, disagreements, new pages).
Teach Radeef something new: a line added to a topic (`as: topic`, `topic`, `text`) or a question and its answer (`as: faq`, `question`, `answer`, optional `topic`); answers what was saved.
endpoints.description: 422 `topic_full` when the topic would pass its length, `faqs_full` past 300 FAQs.

endpoints.summary: Before teaching Radeef a line (`text`), read which topic it belongs to; or check a link (`url`) is on the business's own site and can be read. Saves nothing.
Settle a disagreement Radeef noticed: the figure of side `a` or `b` of the notice `key` becomes what it knows for sure; answers the chosen figure and the notices left.
endpoints.description: 404 for a disagreement not noticed now; 422 `topic_full` or `source_state`.

endpoints.summary: List what Radeef noticed in its knowledge and waits on the owner: pages to confirm, missing or unconfirmed policies customers asked about, two places disagreeing on a figure (settle with radeef.notices.choose), new pages.

Examine Radeef: ten questions from its own knowledge and hard cases, each answered and judged; queued: answers the thread's message to poll with radeef.owner.message. Missed questions can be answered with radeef.unanswered.answer.
endpoints.description: Three a day (429 `exams`), ten of the playground's daily messages (429 `daily`); 422 `empty_knowledge`, 503 `unavailable`.

endpoints.summary: Read one message of the person's owner thread again: a rehearsal or an exam fills its message while it runs, so poll it until it is done.
Rehearse Radeef on up to three (`count`) real questions customers asked, answered as a customer would be answered; queued: answers the thread's message to poll with radeef.owner.message.
endpoints.description: Takes the playground's daily messages. Nothing reaches a customer.

endpoints.summary: Start a new owner thread with Radeef (the open one is closed); answers the fresh brief.

Talk with Radeef as its owner (`text`: ask what it knows, how it would answer, or tell it something to learn); answers its reply and any change cards it proposes (apply them with radeef.owner_changes.apply).
endpoints.description: Nothing changes until a card is applied. Refusals: 429 `daily` (30 a day), `monthly` (300 a month per account) or `busy`; 503 `unavailable` or `failed`.

endpoints.summary: Read owner mode: the brief of what Radeef knows and lacks, the person's open thread with Radeef, the change cards waiting to be applied, and the messages left.
Apply a change card Radeef proposed in owner mode (optionally with `edits` to its question, answer, topic, text, to or word); answers the card, applied.
endpoints.description: 409 with the card when it was applied, dismissed, went stale or expired already. Undo with radeef.owner_changes.undo.

endpoints.summary: Dismiss a change card Radeef proposed in owner mode; answers the card.
Undo an applied change card: the value before is written back, while what it wrote still stands; answers the card.
endpoints.description: 409 `not_applied` or `changed_since`.

endpoints.summary: Add a page of the business's website for Radeef to read (`url`, https); it is read in the background: answers the source, `state` reading until then (radeef.sources.show).
endpoints.description: 422 `pages_full` (30 pages), `duplicate_page`, `not_https`. A whole site is read with radeef.scans.create. A page's facts are only described until confirmed (radeef.sources.confirm).

endpoints.summary: Remove a website page and what Radeef read from it; answers ok.
Read a website page of Radeef's again now, in the background; answers the source.

Try a topic's text before saving it: Radeef answers `question` (else the question customers ask most on that `topic`) from `text` as typed; answers the reply and the question. Nothing is saved or sent.
endpoints.description: Counts against the playground's day. Save the text with radeef.topics.update. 422 `invalid_topic` when no question is given and none was asked on the topic.

endpoints.summary: Start a new test conversation in the playground (the person's open one is closed); answers ok.

Write to Radeef as a customer (`text`; `phone` a real customer's number to try order questions) and get how it would answer: the reply parts or the handoff to the team with its reason, the sources and tools it used, the `turn_id`. Nothing is sent to anyone, nothing is charged.
endpoints.description: Messages continue the person's test conversation until radeef.playground.reset. A handoff for missing knowledge is answered with radeef.unanswered.answer (its `turn_id`). Refusals: 422 `empty_knowledge` (teach it first), 429 `daily` (100 a day per application) or `busy`, 503 `unavailable` or `failed`, 403 `phone_not_allowed`, 422 `invalid_phone`.

endpoints.summary: Read the playground: the day's messages left, whether Radeef knows anything yet, whether a real customer's phone may be used for order questions, suggested questions (from its knowledge, and hard cases), and the person's open test conversation.
List the store's products Radeef knows (Salla or Zid), ten a page, searched by name or code with `q`.
endpoints.description: `next_cursor` is the next page's number. Read the catalogue again with radeef.store.sync.

endpoints.summary: Set aside one proposal of a reading (it stays among the set-aside ones, to restore); answers its id and status.
Bring a set-aside proposal back to the review; answers its id and status.

Apply the owner's choices on what a reading found: `kept` (proposal ids that become knowledge), `rejected`, `edits`, `merge` (append or replace a topic's text), `follow` (pages to keep reading), `add_pages`, `vanished` (keep or delete); answers the result and the review left.
endpoints.description: What is kept is what Radeef tells customers from then on; `vanished: delete` removes pages.

endpoints.summary: Read what readings of the site found and wait for the owner: the proposals by topic with their facts and quotes, how sure each is, the text Radeef holds there, the set-aside ones, and a re-read's new and vanished pages.
endpoints.description: Keep or set aside proposals with radeef.review.apply.

endpoints.summary: Start reading the business's website for Radeef (`url`, `mine: true` for a site that is not the store's or the reviewed one); answers the reading. Poll radeef.scans.show, then radeef.review.show.
endpoints.description: One at a time (409 `scan_running`), three a day (429 `scan_daily`); 422 `not_https`, `not_your_site`.

endpoints.summary: Resume a stopped or failed reading of the site from where it stopped; answers the reading.
endpoints.description: 409 `scan_state` for a reading that cannot be resumed.

endpoints.summary: Read a reading of the site: its status (running until done, stopped or failed), its counts, each page with its state, and what it proposed.
Stop a reading of the site that is running; what it read so far stays for review. Answers the reading.
endpoints.description: 409 `scan_state` for a reading not running.

endpoints.summary: Read what a reading of the site would start from (the address and where it came from), the latest reading, and the readings left today.
Read Radeef's settings: every section (persona, pace, handoff, hours, limits, store) in the shape radeef.settings.update takes, the mode, the character and the price per conversation.
Save one section of Radeef's settings (`persona`, `pace`, `handoff`, `hours`, `limits` or `store`), the whole section as radeef.settings.show answers it; answers the settings.
endpoints.description: Each section takes only its own fields (the input lists every section's together). `hours` with a `week` also writes the Tawked Chat inbox's working hours first: 502 `hours_save_failed` when Tawked Chat refuses (nothing changed). `limits.monthly_cap_halalas` caps the month's spend; past it Radeef pauses.

endpoints.summary: Set when Radeef answers: `hours_mode` (always, outside the team's hours, inside them) with `mode` (live answers customers, draft suggests to the team); answers Radeef.
endpoints.description: With Radeef on, `mode: live` answers real customers from their next message.

endpoints.summary: Choose Radeef's character from the deck (`character`) and its name (`persona_name`, optional `persona_name_en`); answers Radeef.
endpoints.description: The deck's keys are in radeef.setup.show and radeef.settings.show (`characters`); `custom` keeps fields set in the persona settings and saves only the name.

endpoints.summary: Confirm a fact of the setup's brief as right: the topic's text (shipping, returns, payment, warranty, contact, about) stands as Radeef holds it; answers the setup.
endpoints.description: 422 `nothing_to_confirm` for a topic with no text.

endpoints.summary: Turn Radeef on to answer customers: `choice` always (every hour), outside (only outside the team's hours) or suggest (draft replies for the team only); answers Radeef with its state.
endpoints.description: With `always` or `outside`, Radeef answers the application's real WhatsApp customers from their next message. Refusals: 409 `cannot_turn_on` (answered before any approval is asked), 502 `switch_failed` (nothing changed).

endpoints.summary: Start reading the business's website for Radeef (`url`, `mine: true` when it is not the store's or the reviewed site); answers the reading, which runs for a few minutes: poll radeef.scans.show, then review what it found with radeef.review.show.
endpoints.description: Refusals: 409 `scan_running`, 429 `scan_daily` (three a day), 422 `not_https` or `not_your_site`. Also connects the store when its app is installed.

endpoints.summary: Read Radeef's setup: the current move (read, character, meet), the site address to read and the latest reading, the character deck and the chosen one, the brief of what it learned, and how it may go live.
Confirm a read website page's text as facts Radeef may state (prices, policies), not just describe; answers the source.
endpoints.description: 422 `source_state` for anything but a page with readable text.

endpoints.summary: Remove a source from what Radeef knows (any kind); a read page's address is never read again. Answers ok.

List what Radeef knows from, ten a page: FAQs, corrections, website pages and files, each with its kind, title, tier, topic, state (confirmed, reference, needs_confirm, reading, review, unreadable, gone, off) and uses; filter by `type`, `tier`, `topic`, `state`, `q`.
endpoints.description: `next_cursor` is the next page's number. A source's detail is radeef.sources.show.

endpoints.summary: Stop Radeef using a source (`enabled: false`) or use it again (`enabled: true`), without deleting it; answers the source.

Read one source of Radeef's knowledge (an FAQ, a correction, a page or a file): its state, what Radeef takes from it, its text or question and answer, passages, versions, the customer questions it answered and any disagreement.
Turn Radeef on (`enabled: true`, optionally with `mode` live or draft) or off, or switch only its `mode`; answers Radeef with its new state.
endpoints.description: On and live, Radeef answers the application's real WhatsApp customers from its next message; draft only writes suggestions for the team. Refusals: 409 `cannot_turn_on` (locked or no model: read radeef.agent.show; answered before any approval is asked), 502 `switch_failed` (Tawked Chat did not accept it; nothing changed). Test answers with radeef.playground.send first.

endpoints.summary: Read the store Radeef answers from (Salla or Zid): whether it is connected, its products and when they were last read, and which store tools (orders, order status, products) are on.
Read the store's product catalogue again for Radeef now (Salla or Zid), queued; answers ok. Follow it with radeef.store.show.
endpoints.description: 404 `no_store` when the application holds no store. Six a hour.

endpoints.summary: List the topics Radeef knows the business by (shipping, returns, payment, warranty, contact, about), each with its text, its state (known, incomplete, unknown), what is missing and what customers asked about it. The six topics in one answer (no paging).
Read one topic of Radeef's knowledge: its text and state, what is missing, where each line came from, what customers asked about it in 30 days, its FAQs and a change a re-read proposes.
Replace a topic's text (`text`, null or empty clears it): what Radeef says about shipping, returns, payment, warranty, contact, or the business (about); answers the topic.
endpoints.description: At most 2,000 characters (about: 3,000). Preview the answer before saving with radeef.playground.preview.

endpoints.summary: Answer a question Radeef could not (its `turn_id`, from radeef.unanswered.list, a playground reply or an exam): the `answer` (and optionally the `question` reworded) becomes an FAQ, and every customer who asked it is marked answered; answers the FAQ and how many questions it closed.
endpoints.description: An FAQ already asking it has its answer replaced (`updated: true`). 422 `invalid_question` when no question is given and the run has none left.

endpoints.summary: List the questions Radeef could not answer and handed to the team, grouped, the most asked first: the question, how many asked it, its other wordings, its topic, and the `turn_id` to answer it with radeef.unanswered.answer.
endpoints.description: `period`: today, 7d, 30d (default) or month. The 50 most asked, `limit` at a time (`cursor` the next page).

endpoints.summary: List the Salla and Zid stores this token reaches: platform, name, status, linked application, whether any notification is on and whether checkout consent is attested. Open one with stores.salla.show or stores.zid.show.
endpoints.description: `?platform=salla|zid` narrows the list. A store with `application_id: null` waits for its application: link it with stores.<platform>.setup.link.

endpoints.summary: Turn on, at once, the chosen notifications of a Salla store on its first visit (nothing on yet); answers how many are on. The store then messages its customers on each event.
endpoints.description: Body: `slots`, the slots to turn on (`order_confirmed`, `order_status:shipped`…), from `stores.salla.show`'s rows. Refusals: already_active (change them one by one with stores.salla.kinds.update), nothing_chosen, needs_mapping (with `slots`), no_number, store_not_active.

endpoints.summary: Change what the Tawked Chat team sees and does with the Salla store's orders (the orders tab: customer, orders, status changes); answers the settings as saved.
Save the chat button on the Salla store's own pages, whole (on or off, position, colours, greeting); answers the button as saved. Turning it on needs a number that takes messages.
Say (`attested: true`) or withdraw that the Salla store's checkout collects its customers' consent to marketing messages; answers the consent as it stands.
endpoints.description: A statement for the business, by the owner or an admin, recorded with who and when. Given, the store's marketing reaches its customers without each one subscribing, and its customers already in Contacts are subscribed. Saying again what is said changes nothing.

endpoints.summary: Add the chosen Salla employees to the application's support team (`as: support`, they answer in Tawked Chat) or as members of the account (`as: member`); answers each person's outcome.
endpoints.description: Body: `people`, each `{salla_user_id, as}`, ids from stores.salla.employees.list. Name and mobile are Salla's, never the request's. An outcome is `added`, `exists`, or why not. 503 `salla_unavailable` when Salla could not be read: nobody was added.

endpoints.summary: List the employees Salla names for the application's store, each with their state in Tawked (none, support, member, …); answers `people`, `error` (denied, unavailable or null) and whether this person may add them.
endpoints.description: Mobiles and e-mails are whole only for who may add (the owner or an admin who manages the store); masked otherwise. Salla's list is kept a few minutes: stores.salla.employees.refresh reads it again.

endpoints.summary: Read the store's employees from Salla again now (after someone was added or changed in Salla); answers the list as stores.salla.employees.list does.

Change one notification of a Salla store at once: switch it on or off, choose its template (the kit's or the number's own), map the template's placeholders, set its options. Answers the slot as it was before.
endpoints.description: Body: `status` (the order status, required for order_status), `enabled`, `template` `{source: kit|own, name?}`, `mapping` `{body: {placeholder: fact|text:…|null}, header, button}`, `options` (cart reminders, cash on delivery, rating). Turning a notification on sends WhatsApp messages to the store's customers on each matching event. Refusals: needs_mapping (with `missing`), template_unusable, templates_unavailable, unknown_slot, unknown_source, text_too_long, no_choice, store_not_active.

endpoints.summary: Submit to Meta the kit templates the store's enabled notifications still need; answers how many were created and which failed. Meta reviews each one: `next` says how to follow it (stores.salla.templates.refresh, then stores.salla.show).
Change a Salla store's settings: the language its messages go in, English variants, quiet hours, pause. Answers ok.
Link a Salla store waiting for its application to one of the account's applications (`application_id`), or to a new one named after the store (null); answers the application's id.
endpoints.description: For the account's owner and admins. The store sends from that application's WhatsApp number once linked; it cannot be moved back. Refusals: not_linkable, unknown_application, application_limit, account_inactive, link_expired, application_taken; not_linkable before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: Leave the WhatsApp number for later in a Salla store's setup (`later`, true when absent), so its notifications list opens before the number; answers ok.

Read one Salla store as the console shows it: its status and application, its setup (link and number), every notification row with its state and template, settings, consent, chat button and chat orders tab.
endpoints.description: Each row of `notifications.rows` is a slot (`order_confirmed`, or `order_status:shipped`): `enabled`, `state` (working, pending, off, missing, mapping, refused, paused, draft…), its `template` (the kit's or the number's own) and the `kit` template's state at Meta. `notifications` is null until the store is active and linked: follow `setup.steps`. `next` says what the notifications need now, from their `attention` (e.g. `create_kit`: stores.salla.kit_templates.create; a mapping or a rejected template: stores.salla.kinds.update), the same call me.show's store step names. `billing` only for who sees money.

endpoints.summary: Read the store number's templates from Meta again (after Meta approved or rejected one); answers ok with a `next` (read the store again), or templates_unavailable when Meta did not answer.
Send a test store notification to the account owner's own phone (never a customer), from the store's number; answers ok.
endpoints.description: At most three an hour. Refusals: no_owner_phone, no_number (with the connect human_action), too_many_tests, store_not_active; each answered before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: Turn on, at once, the chosen notifications of a Zid store on its first visit (nothing on yet); answers how many are on. The store then messages its customers on each event.
endpoints.description: Body: `slots`, the slots to turn on (`order_confirmed`, `order_status:shipped`…), from `stores.zid.show`'s rows. Refusals: already_active (change them one by one with stores.zid.kinds.update), nothing_chosen, needs_mapping (with `slots`), no_number, store_not_active.

endpoints.summary: Save the chat button on the Zid store's own pages, whole (on or off, position, colours, greeting); answers the button as saved. Turning it on needs a number that takes messages.
Say (`attested: true`) or withdraw that the Zid store's checkout collects its customers' consent to marketing messages; answers the consent as it stands.
endpoints.description: A statement for the business, by the owner or an admin, recorded with who and when. Given, the store's marketing reaches its customers without each one subscribing. Saying again what is said changes nothing.

endpoints.summary: Change one notification of a Zid store at once: switch it on or off, choose its template (the kit's or the number's own), map the template's placeholders, set its options. Answers the slot as it was before.
endpoints.description: Body: `status` (the order status, required for order_status), `enabled`, `template` `{source: kit|own, name?}`, `mapping` `{body: {placeholder: fact|text:…|null}, header, button}`, `options` (cart reminders, cash on delivery). Turning a notification on sends WhatsApp messages to the store's customers on each matching event. Refusals: needs_mapping (with `missing`), template_unusable, templates_unavailable, unknown_slot, unknown_source, text_too_long, no_choice, store_not_active.

endpoints.summary: Submit to Meta the kit templates the store's enabled notifications still need; answers how many were created and which failed. Meta reviews each one: `next` says how to follow it (stores.zid.templates.refresh, then stores.zid.show).
Change a Zid store's settings: the language its messages go in, English variants, quiet hours, pause. Answers ok.
Link a Zid store waiting for its application to one of the account's applications (`application_id`), or to a new one named after the store (null); answers the application's id.
endpoints.description: For the account's owner and admins. The store sends from that application's WhatsApp number once linked; it cannot be moved back. Refusals: not_linkable, unknown_application, application_limit, account_inactive, link_expired, application_taken; not_linkable before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: Leave the WhatsApp number for later in a Zid store's setup (`later`, true when absent), so its notifications list opens before the number; answers ok.
Read one Zid store as the console shows it: its status and application, its setup (link and number), every notification row with its state and template, settings, consent and chat button.
endpoints.description: Each row of `notifications.rows` is a slot (`order_confirmed`, or `order_status:shipped`): `enabled`, `state` (working, pending, off, missing, mapping, refused, paused, draft…), its `template` (the kit's or the number's own) and the `kit` template's state at Meta. `notifications` is null until the store is active and linked: follow `setup.steps`. `next` says what the notifications need now, from their `attention` (e.g. `create_kit`: stores.zid.kit_templates.create; a mapping or a rejected template: stores.zid.kinds.update), the same call me.show's store step names. `billing` only for who sees money.

endpoints.summary: Read the store number's templates from Meta again (after Meta approved or rejected one); answers ok with a `next` (read the store again), or templates_unavailable when Meta did not answer.
Send a test store notification to the account owner's own phone (never a customer), from the store's number; answers ok.
endpoints.description: At most three an hour. Refusals: no_owner_phone, no_number (with the connect human_action), too_many_tests, store_not_active; each answered before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: The application's Verify settings (code length, how long a code lives, attempts, rate limits, autofill, the spike guard; the daily spend cap for who sees the money) with each one's bounds, and the pumping guard's pause.
Change some of the application's Verify settings (only the fields sent; null clears one that may be empty), in the names verify.settings.show answers; answers the settings.
endpoints.description: Each value must sit within its bounds (verify.settings.show), else 422 `invalid_settings` naming the `fields`. `autofill_domain` comes from the reviewed website and is never set. The spend cap is money: only who manages the wallet may send `daily_spend_cap_halalas` (403 otherwise).

endpoints.summary: Check the code the owner's phone received for a test verification (`id` from verify.test.send, `code`), as the public API would (POST /v1/verify/check); answers the API's `response` (its `status`: verified or not).

Send a test code to the account owner's own phone through the application's test key, as the public API would (POST /v1/verify/start); answers the API's `response`, the key used (its `plaintext` only when this call created it) and `seconds_left`. Then call verify.test.check.
endpoints.description: The sandbox reaches only the owner's verified phone, whatever is asked, with a daily cap. 409 `verify_off` while the application does not have Verify (the console offers no test then): its `next` turns it on with applications.products.add. Otherwise refused as the API would: 402 `insufficient_credits` (with the top-up's `human_action`), `account_not_active` (403), `application_paused`, `sandbox_unverified_destination`, `sandbox_quota_exceeded`; 409 `busy` while another test send of the application is on its way.

endpoints.summary: The application's Verify usage for a `period` (today, 7d, month, 30d; Riyadh time) against the same span before: codes sent, delivered, verified, expired, failed, not delivered (refunded), the verified rate, and what the wallet was charged (`charged_halalas`, for who sees the money).

The application's verification log, newest first, narrowed by `status` (waiting, verified, failed, expired, canceled), `mode` (live, test), `range` (today, 7d, 30d, 90d) and `q`: each code's masked number, status, attempts, key, times; its price for who sees the money.
One verification of the application by its id (from verify.test.send or verify.verifications.list): its status, masked number, attempts, key and times; its price for who sees the money.
The auto top-up as set (on or off, the threshold and the amount in halalas, the card, failures and why it turned itself off), or null while Tawked does not offer it or it was never set.
Turn the auto top-up on or off and set its threshold, amount and saved card (`enabled`, `threshold_halalas`, `amount_halalas`, `payment_method_id`); answers the setting.
endpoints.description: On, the saved card is charged on its own whenever the balance falls under the threshold, at most the daily cap a day. A card is saved by the person paying once on the Top up page with «save card» (`wallet.topups.link`). Refusals 422: `unavailable`, `threshold_out_of_range`, `amount_out_of_range`, `card_required`, `card_expired`, each answered before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: The account's prepaid balance as Wallet › Balance shows it, in halalas: the balance and its state (`ok`, `low`, `out`), about how many codes it buys, this month's spend and its projection, how long it lasts, the low-balance alert, the auto top-up and the card on file (masked), the month by product, and the last top-up.
endpoints.description: To add credit, call `wallet.topups.link` and hand the link to the person, or ask for a bank transfer's proforma with `wallet.proformas.create`.

endpoints.summary: The account's billing details (legal name, VAT number, the national address, the billing e-mail), whether they are complete, and whether a top-up must ask for them first.
endpoints.description: The details themselves (`profile`) only for a person who may manage the wallet, as in the console.

endpoints.summary: Save the account's billing details, the ones every invoice is addressed to (legal name, city, e-mail, and while Tawked is VAT-registered the national address); answers the billing details.
The account's billing documents, newest first: invoices, credit notes and proformas, each with its number, kind, status, totals and VAT in halalas, and its PDF's address.
endpoints.description: Filters: `number` (a prefix), `document_kind` (`invoice`, `credit_note`, `proforma`), `document_month` (YYYY-MM, Riyadh). Paged by `limit` and `cursor`. The PDF address is the console's, for a signed-in person.

endpoints.summary: One billing document: its number, kind, status, totals, VAT and discount in halalas, who it is addressed to, what a credit note corrects, what a settled proforma led to, and its PDF's address.
Remove a saved card, at the card processor and here; an auto top-up that charged it turns off. Answers ok.

The cards saved for the auto top-up, newest first, masked as the console shows them: brand, last four digits, expiry, whether expired. Empty while Tawked does not offer auto top-up. Every card in one answer (no paging).
Cancel an open proforma (the transfer will not be expected); answers the proforma, now cancelled.
endpoints.description: 409 `not_open` once it was settled or cancelled, before any approval is asked. A cancelled proforma is never reopened: ask for a new one.

endpoints.summary: Ask for a proforma to top up by bank transfer (`amount_halalas`, the credit wanted); answers the proforma with its number, total and PDF. The balance moves only once Tawked's team settles the transfer.
endpoints.description: A first payer may send `billing` (legal_name, city, email, and the national address while Tawked is VAT-registered), saved first. Refusals: 422 `invalid_amount` (outside the transfer's bounds, `wallet.topups.link` names them), 409 `billing_profile_incomplete`, `transfers_unavailable`, `open_proformas_limit`, 503 `invoicing_unavailable`.

endpoints.summary: The wallet's settings: the low-balance alert (threshold in halalas, the e-mail, the WhatsApp number it goes to, masked) and, while Tawked offers it, the auto top-up (its setting, today's charges against the daily cap, the saved cards masked, the bounds).

Save the wallet's settings in one go, as Balance's save bar does: the low-balance alert (`alert_enabled`, `alert_threshold_halalas`, `alert_email`) and optionally the auto top-up (`auto_topup`: enabled, threshold, amount, card); answers the settings.
endpoints.description: With `auto_topup.enabled` true the saved card is charged on its own whenever the balance falls under the threshold (at most the daily cap a day). A refused auto top-up saves nothing (422 with its fields under `auto_topup.*`: `threshold_out_of_range`, `amount_out_of_range`, `card_required`, `card_expired`, `unavailable`).

endpoints.summary: The wallet's ledger lines, newest first: each one's kind (topup, otp_charge, whatsapp_message_charge, email_charge, chat_agent_charge, refund, adjustment, signup_bonus…), product, application, template, a reference the client knows, the signed amount and the balance after, in halalas.
endpoints.description: Filters: `reference` (a prefix), `kind`, `product`, `application` (an application id), `month` (YYYY-MM, Riyadh), `day` (YYYY-MM-DD), and on a partner account `side` (`own` or `clients`). Paged by `limit` and `cursor`. A token chosen for some applications reads only their lines and the wallet's own (top-ups, adjustments); `balance_after_halalas` stays the whole wallet's. One month summed: wallet.statements.show.

endpoints.summary: One month's statement (YYYY-MM, Riyadh): the opening and closing balance, the top-ups, the usage by product, the refunds and adjustments, the month day by day, and the address of its PDF.
endpoints.description: A month the account had no wallet in is 404. On a partner account `side` (`own` or `clients`) narrows the usage to that side; the balances stay the whole wallet's. A token chosen for some applications sums only their usage and refunds. The months there are: `periods`.

endpoints.summary: The console's Top up address for the person to pay by card (optionally with `amount_halalas` filled in), and the amounts it offers: the packages, the range, the bounds. Relay `human_action` (what to say, the link in the person's language); read `wallet.balance.show` after they paid.
endpoints.description: A card payment happens on the payment page in the person's own browser: no operation charges a new card. The amount must be one some way to pay takes (422 `amount_out_of_range`); with no way to pay on at all, `payments_available` is false, `url` null, `packages` empty and the `human_action` is `payments_unavailable` (the person is told topping up is not open now; read this again later), and an amount answers 503 `payments_unavailable` with it. Every top-up `human_action` elsewhere (402 `insufficient_credits`, 409 `insufficient_balance`) is that same `payments_unavailable` while no way to pay is on. `url` is in the person's language, as the human_action's. `can_pay` is true when this person may pay (their role manages the wallet) and a way to pay is on: false while `payments_available` is false, and for a role that may not pay (its human_action then asks the owner). Paying needs a person who may manage the wallet, and billing details first (`billing_required_before_topup`, set them with `wallet.billing.update`).

endpoints.summary: Ask Meta again whether the number's WhatsApp Business Account has a payment method; answers `billing_state` (ready, missing or unknown), and while it is missing the `human_action` that adds one at Meta.
endpoints.description: The payment method is added by a person on Meta's billing page (`human_action.url`, also whatsapp.number.show's `billing_url`): relay `human_action.say`, then call this again. Held to 10 a minute per person, shared with the console.

endpoints.summary: What Meta charged on the application's WhatsApp number this month and last, by Meta's category (MARKETING, UTILITY, AUTHENTICATION, SERVICE for the replies past the free ones), with an estimate where Meta keeps the amount from Tawked, and the number's free replies this month.
endpoints.description: Read from Meta's pricing analytics, at most once an hour. `charges.months[].categories[]`: `volume` is the messages Meta charged, `cost` Meta's amount in `charges.currency`, null when Meta keeps it from Tawked (`charges.cost_shown` false: the number's WhatsApp account is the business's own); then `estimate` is those messages times Meta's published Saudi price for the month, and `unpriced` the charged messages with no known price. An estimate is never the bill: the exact amount is in the invoices at Meta. A free reply is never charged and never counted here. `free_replies` is the number's free replies this month: the `allowance`, `used`, `left` and `renews_on`; past it Meta charges each reply. `tawked_fee_halalas` is Tawked's own fee per template message, charged from the balance (whatsapp.usage.show sums it). `charges` or `free_replies` is null while Meta cannot be read.

endpoints.summary: Disconnect the application's WhatsApp number from Tawked: its Tawked Chat inbox goes, sending stops until a number is connected again (whatsapp.connection.link). Answers ok.
endpoints.description: The number is not deregistered from Meta and its templates stay on the WhatsApp Business Account. 503 `meta_unavailable` or `inbox_unavailable` when a step could not run: nothing changed, retry.

endpoints.summary: Where the person connects the application's WhatsApp number (the console address that opens Meta's window), and how far it got: connected or not, the stage, the person's signup in flight.
endpoints.description: Connecting a number is done by a person in Meta's Embedded Signup window (Meta's rule): until `connected` is true, `human_action` says what to tell them and the link they open (the owner's, by name, when this person's role may not connect it); then read this or whatsapp.number.show again.

endpoints.summary: Make a live application key for the sending API (named "First message"); answers the key's plaintext once, and its prefix.
endpoints.description: The plaintext is in this answer only: store it. A live key sends real messages billed to the balance. 409 `application_not_active` once the application is rejected or suspended, before any approval is asked.

endpoints.summary: Send the guide's template to the token's person's own phone, as the application (Meta bills it); answers the message with its status. Poll whatsapp.first_message.show for delivery.
endpoints.description: Only to the person's own phone, never a number the caller gives. One at a time: while a test is on its way, the answer is that one. 409 with the phase that stops it (`setting_up`, `payment` with the pay_meta human_action, `blocked`), `no_template`, `busy`; 422 `no_phone`; all but `busy` answered before any approval is asked. Held to 6 per 10 minutes, shared with the console.

endpoints.summary: Where the number stands on the way to its first message: the phase (setting up, payment, blocked, ready…), the template a test sends and the request that sends it from your servers, and the last test with its delivery status.
endpoints.description: Poll it after whatsapp.first_message.send_test until `message.status` is delivered, read or failed. `next` says what the phase waits for.

endpoints.summary: Re-read every go-live fact from Meta (payment method, display name, business verification, health, an approved template, a first message, the badge); answers the checklist, each item done, to do, blocked or unknown with where to act.

List the WhatsApp messages the application sent, newest first, each with its masked destination, template, status (accepted, sent, delivered, read, failed with Meta's error) and times; filter by status (or `in_flight`), period (`range`: today, 7d, 30d, 90d; default 30d), template, or a reference or phone (`q`).

Render a WhatsApp template message exactly as whatsapp.messages.send would send it, sending nothing: the message with its buttons, every check (number, recipient, template APPROVED, values, consent, account, balance), the price (Tawked's fee and Meta's estimate for MARKETING), `problems` that block it and `warnings` to show the person. The body is whatsapp.messages.send's.
endpoints.description: `ready` is true when nothing blocks the send. A request that cannot be rendered at all answers its code: 409 `whatsapp_not_connected` (a person connects the number: human_action), 422 `invalid_destination`, `template_not_found`, `language_required` (with `languages`), `template_not_approved`, `template_authentication`, `template_image_header`, `template_unsupported`, `invalid_params` (with `expected`); 503 `meta_unavailable`. A balance short of the fee is a problem with a top-up human_action.

endpoints.summary: Send one APPROVED WhatsApp template to a customer from the application's number; answers the message (status `accepted`, then poll whatsapp.messages.show for sent, delivered, read or failed). Charges Tawked's fee from the wallet.
endpoints.description: The public API's send, as the application (its internal "Account API" key): `to` the customer's number (05… or +9665…), `template` and `language` (or `lang`, the Sending API's name) an APPROVED template (whatsapp.templates.list), `params` an object keyed by the placeholder (`{"1": "1042"}`, or `{"order": "1042"}` for a named one), `header` the header's variable, `buttons` [{index, parameter}] for a URL button's variable, `reference` your own id. Every gate of a send holds: the consent of a MARKETING template's recipient, Meta's rules, the wallet. Errors: 409 `insufficient_balance` (with `human_action`: the top-up a person makes), 409 `whatsapp_not_connected` and 403 `whatsapp_unavailable` (a `human_action` when a person can lift it), the send refusals by the codes whatsapp.messages.preview answers (e.g. 422 `invalid_destination`, `template_not_found`, `template_not_approved`, `template_unsupported`, `invalid_params`, `consent_opted_out`), the same before an approval and at the send, 503 `meta_unavailable`. With the token's approvals on, every refusal whatsapp.messages.preview finds (a recipient that is not a Saudi mobile, a template not there or not APPROVED, values that do not fit it, a recipient who stopped marketing, the balance) is answered before the person is asked to approve. For many recipients, a campaign (campaigns.campaigns.create) is the way.

endpoints.summary: One WhatsApp message the application sent, by its id: its status and the time of each step, Meta's error when it failed, the text the customer read, the key that sent it, and `next`: poll while it is accepted or sent, what a failure means.
Set the number's two-step verification PIN on Meta (six digits); answers ok.
Read the number's facts, health, quality and account again from Meta (the console's "check again"); answers the number as whatsapp.number.show does.
endpoints.description: Held to 10 a minute per person, shared with the console.

endpoints.summary: Ask Meta to change the number's display name (the name customers see); Meta reviews it against the business. Answers the number and `next`: read whatsapp.number.show once or twice a day for `new_name_status`.
endpoints.description: Goes to Meta for review and replaces the name customers see once approved.

endpoints.summary: Request Meta's verified badge (Official Business Account) for the number: the website, country, language, five to ten links that show the business is notable; answers the number with `oba_status` and `next` (read whatsapp.number.show once a day until Meta decides).
endpoints.description: Read `oba_can_request` and `oba_blockers` on whatsapp.number.show first: Meta waits 30 days after a refusal.

endpoints.summary: The application's WhatsApp number: connected or not, its stage and what to do next, display name and its review, quality, messaging tier and limit, business profile, verified badge, Meta billing state and the go-live checklist.
endpoints.description: Read from what Tawked last synced from Meta; call whatsapp.number.refresh first for Meta's latest. What Meta charges and the free replies: whatsapp.charges.show. `connected` false with `number` null before a number is connected: see whatsapp.connection.link.

endpoints.summary: Set what a customer sees on opening the chat: the welcome message switch, up to four prompts and up to thirty commands (name and hint). Answers the number.
Change the business profile customers see on WhatsApp (about, address, description, e-mail, up to two websites, category, a JPG or PNG picture); a field left out stays as it is. Answers the number.

One turn of Tawked's template assistant on a draft: send your message (or `retry: true`) with the draft's state and revision; it writes into the draft and answers what it said (`turns`), the draft and its lint.
endpoints.description: 429 `assistant_busy` or `assistant_throttled` with `retry_after`; 503 `assistant_not_configured`; 422 `authentication_template` (Meta writes those); 424 `assistant_failed` when the model did not answer.

endpoints.summary: Start a template draft: blank (`source: blank`), for the template assistant (`source: assistant`), or a copy of a template on the number by its name (`duplicate`). Answers the draft with its `revision`.
endpoints.description: Then fill it with whatsapp.template_drafts.update (or ask whatsapp.template_drafts.assistant), and send it to Meta with whatsapp.template_drafts.submit. To submit a template in one step, whatsapp.templates.create needs no draft.

endpoints.summary: Delete a template draft (only Tawked's working copy; nothing on Meta changes); answers ok.
List the application's template drafts (not yet submitted to Meta), newest change first, each with its languages and variants; filter by name (`q`).
One template draft in full: its variants, `revision` (send it back on update and submit), and `lint`, the checks it must pass before Meta sees it (an `error` blocks submit).

Save the draft (same body as update) and submit it to Meta, one template per language; answers the templates created (each id and status) and the languages Meta refused, with its words. Then poll whatsapp.templates.show per id.
endpoints.description: 422 `draft_not_submittable` with `lint` while a check still fails; 409 `stale` when the revision moved; 409 `draft_busy` while another submit of it runs.

endpoints.summary: Save a draft's whole state (name, category, variants per language with header, body, footer, buttons, examples) under the `revision` last read; answers the draft with its new revision and its `lint`; once no `lint` error is left, send it to Meta with whatsapp.template_drafts.submit.
endpoints.description: 409 `stale` with the draft as it now is when someone saved it since your revision: merge and send again with its revision.

endpoints.summary: Create a template from Meta's library: the library row's name and language, the new template's name, one input per library button in its order (a link's base, a phone number). Answers the new template's id, status and `next` (poll whatsapp.templates.show while it is PENDING).
endpoints.description: Find the row with whatsapp.template_library.list. 422 `library_name: libraryUnknown` when the row is not in the library, `buttons…: buttonsMismatch` when the inputs do not match its buttons.

package_name.description: Only when `buttons.*.type` is OTP. Only when `buttons.*.otp_type` is ONE_TAP or ZERO_TAP.

signature_hash.description: Only when `buttons.*.type` is OTP. Only when `buttons.*.otp_type` is ONE_TAP or ZERO_TAP.

zero_tap_terms_accepted.description: Only when `buttons.*.type` is OTP. Only when `buttons.*.otp_type` is ZERO_TAP.

endpoints.summary: Browse Meta's template library (ready-made utility templates Meta usually approves at once), filtered by topic, use case, industry, language or words (`q`); each with the name and buttons whatsapp.template_library.create takes.
endpoints.description: Held to 30 reads a minute per person, shared with the console (429 `rate_limited` past it).

endpoints.summary: Upload a sample image for a template's IMAGE header (multipart `image`, a JPG or PNG of at most 5 MB); answers its `path`, sent as `header_sample` to whatsapp.templates.create or a draft's variant.

Turn the picked suggestions of a finished run (`keys`) into drafts and submit them to Meta; answers each one's outcome (submitted, partial or failed, with the templates created). Then poll whatsapp.templates.show per created id.
endpoints.description: A call makes what fits in its time; suggestions left picked are made on the next call. 409 `suggestions_busy` while another action holds the run.

endpoints.summary: Make one suggestion of a finished run a template draft (or answer the draft it already has), to edit before submitting; answers the draft.
endpoints.description: 404 when the run holds no such key, or Meta already took the suggestion.

endpoints.summary: The application's latest run of template suggestions from the business: its status (queued, reading, writing, done, failed), the business profile, and each suggested template with its key, variants and outcome; plus the runs left today.
endpoints.description: Poll it every few seconds after whatsapp.template_suggestions.start until status is done or failed. `run` is null before the first run.

endpoints.summary: Start a run of template suggestions from the business's website (`website_url`) and a short description; answers the run (status queued). Poll whatsapp.template_suggestions.show until it is done.
endpoints.description: One of the two is needed unless the application holds a Salla store. 409 `suggestions_running` while a run is under way; 429 `suggestions_day_limit` or `suggestions_minute_limit` with `retry_after`.

endpoints.summary: Check a proposed template with whatsapp.templates.create's own rules before creating it, saving nothing: answers `ready` (no error blocks it) and every problem once (`level` error or warning, `field`, `code`, and `problem`: what is wrong in words). The body is exactly whatsapp.templates.create's (any category, an IMAGE header with its `header_sample`, AUTHENTICATION with its fields); then call whatsapp.templates.create with it.
endpoints.description: Errors are what whatsapp.templates.create would refuse (the same codes); warnings are for judgement (Meta may re-categorise or reject). Works before a number is connected, skipping only the names it would read there.

autofill_text.description: Only when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Not when `otp_type` is COPY_CODE.

phone_number.description: Not when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Only when `buttons.*.type` is PHONE_NUMBER.

url.description: Not when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Only when `buttons.*.type` is URL.

header_sample.description: Not when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Only when `header_format` is IMAGE or DOCUMENT.

package_name.description: Only when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Not when `otp_type` is COPY_CODE.

signature_hash.description: Only when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Not when `otp_type` is COPY_CODE.

zero_tap_terms_accepted.description: Only when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Only when `otp_type` is ZERO_TAP.

endpoints.summary: Create a WhatsApp template and submit it to Meta for review; answers its id and status (PENDING until Meta decides). Then poll whatsapp.templates.show with the id until the status is APPROVED or REJECTED.
endpoints.description: The console's template form: name (lower-case, digits, underscores), language, category (UTILITY, MARKETING or AUTHENTICATION), an optional text or IMAGE header (an image needs `header_sample`, a path from whatsapp.template_samples.create), body with {{variables}}, footer, buttons, and `examples`: an object of one example per variable, keyed by the variable's key (`{"body:1": "Sara"}`, or `{"body:order_id": "1042"}` for a named one), never a list. Field errors answer 422 with codes; Meta's own refusal (a name already used…) 422 `meta_refused` with its sentence.

autofill_text.description: Only when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Not when `otp_type` is COPY_CODE.

phone_number.description: Not when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Only when `buttons.*.type` is PHONE_NUMBER.

url.description: Not when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Only when `buttons.*.type` is URL.

header_sample.description: Not when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Only when `header_format` is IMAGE or DOCUMENT.

package_name.description: Only when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Not when `otp_type` is COPY_CODE.

signature_hash.description: Only when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Not when `otp_type` is COPY_CODE.

zero_tap_terms_accepted.description: Only when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Only when `otp_type` is ZERO_TAP.

endpoints.summary: Delete one language of a template on Meta; answers ok with its id, name and language. It stops for every application on the same WhatsApp Business Account: read whatsapp.templates.show's `used_by` first.
endpoints.description: Meta keeps the name reserved for a while after a delete. Meta's own sample templates cannot be deleted (409 `meta_sample`).

endpoints.summary: List the WhatsApp templates on the application's number as Meta holds them, each with its id, status (APPROVED, PENDING, REJECTED…), quality, rejection reason and whether it can be sent; filter by status, category, language or a name (`q`).
endpoints.description: Answers 409 `whatsapp_not_connected` before a number is connected (see whatsapp.connection.link). The list is the catalog Tawked caches from Meta; whatsapp.templates.refresh drops it so the next read asks Meta.

endpoints.summary: Drop Tawked's cached copy of the number's templates; answers ok. The next whatsapp.templates.list or whatsapp.templates.show reads them from Meta afresh.

One WhatsApp template by its Meta id: Meta's status (poll this after a create until APPROVED or REJECTED), quality, rejection reason, whether it can be sent and edited, its parts, what sends it today (campaigns, automations), and `next`: what to do in its status.
endpoints.description: Meta usually reviews a new template within minutes, sometimes up to a day: poll every 30 to 60 seconds. `rejected_reason` names Meta's reason when status is REJECTED; fix the template with whatsapp.templates.update or make a new one.

endpoints.summary: Submit Tawked's starter kit (order and shipping updates in Arabic and English) to Meta, skipping names the number already holds; answers how many were created and which failed with Meta's words. Then poll whatsapp.templates.list until Meta approves them.
Resume a template Meta paused for low quality; answers ok, or Meta's refusal when its pause has not ended.
endpoints.description: Only a PAUSED template (409 `template_not_paused` otherwise).

endpoints.summary: Edit a template's content on Meta (its name and language stay); Meta reviews it again. Answers the template's id and status; poll whatsapp.templates.show for Meta's decision.
endpoints.description: Meta lets only an APPROVED, REJECTED or PAUSED template be edited (409 `template_not_editable` otherwise), an approved one at most once a day and ten times a month. The body is the same as whatsapp.templates.create; name and language are ignored.

autofill_text.description: Only when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Not when `otp_type` is COPY_CODE.

phone_number.description: Not when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Only when `buttons.*.type` is PHONE_NUMBER.

url.description: Not when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Only when `buttons.*.type` is URL.

header_sample.description: Not when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Only when `header_format` is IMAGE or DOCUMENT.

package_name.description: Only when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Not when `otp_type` is COPY_CODE.

signature_hash.description: Only when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Not when `otp_type` is COPY_CODE.

zero_tap_terms_accepted.description: Only when `category` is AUTHENTICATION. Only when `otp_type` is ZERO_TAP.

endpoints.summary: The application's WhatsApp template messages for a `period` (today, 7d, month, 30d; Riyadh time) against the same span before: sent, delivered, read, failed, in flight, the delivered and read rates, and Tawked's fees charged (`charged_halalas`, for who sees the money; Meta bills its own charges separately).
